prd.title: The Reservations Desk Answer Layer. A proposal for Major Marine Tours, Seward.
prd.prepared_for: Colby Lawrence, Vice President, and Tom Tougas, Owner
prd.pr_faq_opening:
SEWARD, ALASKA. A guest calls the Major Marine desk on a Tuesday in June and asks whether they can move their cruise, whether the boat they booked takes a wheelchair, and whether the shuttle will pick them up at the hotel. The person answering was hired in March. They give the right answer to all three inside a minute, and they read the guest the sentence your own page already says, word for word. The one question your published rules don't actually cover goes straight to a named person instead of a guess.

That is the whole outcome. Nothing about it is new information to you. Every one of those answers is already written down on majormarine.com, correctly and precisely. The difference is where the answer lives at 4:40 p.m. on a Sunday in the first week of somebody's first season.

Q. Why does this need attention at all, when the policies are already published and the reviews are good?
A. Because the policies being right is not the same as the answer being fast and identical every time it is given, and because three of the four questions where a wrong answer costs the most have nobody downstream to catch a mistake before it reaches a guest or the bank.

Q. What does it cost to find out whether that is even true at Major Marine?
A. Nothing, and you can start this week. The first thing in this proposal is a sheet of paper on the desk. If the counting shows your desk barely escalates anything, that is a finding that saves you the entire project, and we would much rather find it in September than in March.
prd.problem:
Your rules are written down and they are exact. A cruise-only reservation is refundable up to 72 hours prior to departure. Add a hotel and the clock becomes 7 days. Add motorcoach or train and it becomes 21 days. One date change is free up to 24 hours prior, then a re-booking fee of $15 per person applies, and a 3 percent card processing fee is retained on a cancellation. The shuttle needs an advance reservation and at least 24 hours notice, and it is not available for the 8:00 a.m. 6 Hour Kenai Fjords National Park Cruise. Wheelchair access depends on which vessel is running that departure, it is first deck inside the main cabin only, and no vessel takes a motorized wheelchair. A vegetarian sandwich has to be requested at the time of reservation, on the 6 Hour, 7.5 Hour and 8.5 Hour cruises only.

Every one of those is correct, published, and easy to verify when there is time to verify it. The desk is open 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., seven days a week, year round. On August 10th of this season, seven departures leave the Harbor 360 office in a single day. The answers are spread across your refund policy page, your FAQ and your Seward check-in page, roughly thirty public pages in total, and the person on the phone is often somebody hired inside your January 15th to April 15th window who is in their first weeks of their first season while a guest waits on the line.

So the problem is not that anything is wrong on your website. The problem is that four specific questions have a high cost when the answer is wrong, a finite number of correct answers, and no mechanism between a new hire's memory and a guest.
prd.cost_of_being_wrong:
The refund clock is the one that costs cash. Quoting the 72 hour cruise-only clock to a guest who actually holds a 21 day transportation package means refunding money the company did not owe, on a booking whose motorcoach or train seat you may already be committed to. Nobody catches that in the moment. It surfaces after the money has moved, because the wrong clock sounds exactly as authoritative as the right one. The strict direction of the same error is worse in a different way, since refusing a refund the published policy grants is public, on a brand whose position is being the locally owned family company in that harbour.

The accessibility question has no catcher at all upstream of the dock. A guest builds a multi-day Alaska itinerary around a departure, and finds out at the gangway.

The shuttle question is the sharpest chain, and every link in it is your own published rule. A guest is told the shuttle covers the 8:00 a.m. 6 Hour cruise. It doesn't. The terminal loop runs 7:00 a.m. to 9:45 a.m. on a 15 minute headway, which is a partial fallback for a cruise ship guest and none at all for a guest who parked. The walk is 0.6 miles from Harbor 360 and 0.8 from the South Harbor office, with luggage, before an 8:00 a.m. boarding. A guest who misses the sailing is a no-show, and the no-show rule says a ticket not used at the time of sailing is completely non-refundable and may not be used on any other sailing. We want to be precise about that one, because it is easy to dress up as revenue and it isn't. You keep the fare. What that error costs you is goodwill and the reputation you have spent over thirty years building, which is the actual thing you sell against a NYSE-listed competitor in the same harbour.

The dietary question is low dollars and real guest experience, discovered in the galley on the day, when nothing can be fixed.
prd.user:
The primary user is a first-season Customer Service and Sales agent, one of about 60 seasonal staff you hire in the January 15th to April 15th window, in weeks one through six on the phone. They are the whole target. Their failure is not an inability to read your policies, it is not knowing which of roughly thirty pages holds the answer while somebody waits.

The secondary user is whoever they currently interrupt. Right now the escalation path is a veteran, and the cost of a new hire's question is paid by an experienced person's time.

We are being deliberate about who this is NOT for. It is not aimed at Colby Lawrence at 22 years, Kirsten McNeil at 11 or Rodney Roemmich at 15. The strongest independent measurement available on tools of this kind, a field study of 5,179 support agents, found the gains concentrated in novices and close to nothing for experienced staff. We read that for direction and for who to aim at, never as a percentage we would attach to your desk. Rolling this out to everyone would dilute a real effect into an average that looks like failure, so the design and the measurement both aim at the March cohort only.

The buyer is the owner and the Vice President. The engagement also needs a named internal policy owner, which is a different person from the buyer and is named below.
prd.reason_now:
Three reasons, all of them calendar, none of them ours.

First, the observation window closes on October 11th. Your desk only exists while a season runs. There are roughly nine weeks left in the 2026 season, and the question mix changes inside them, since the 8.5 Hour ends September 7th, the 7.5 Hour ends September 13th, the 6 Hour ends September 21st, and the 4 Hour runs alone to October 11th. Miss these weeks and the next chance to count anything is March, by which time the decision to build has to already have been made.

Second, the people this is for are hired between January 15th and April 15th, and the 2027 season opens March 7th. Anything meant to help them has to be in their hands before then, which fixes the whole schedule by working backwards from a date you set, not one we picked.

Third, two seasons are already live on your own pages at the same time. The 4 Hour Kenai Fjords Wildlife Cruise is $149 for 2026 and the 4 Hour Spring Wildlife Cruise is already published at $109 for March to May 2027. So what does the 4 Hour cost already has two correct answers, and that gets harder every year rather than easier.
prd.after_state: A first-season agent answers a refund, an accessibility, a shuttle or a dietary question in their first week, in under a minute, with your published sentence on screen to read out loud, and anything your published rules don't cover is routed to a named person instead of guessed at.
goals: A first-season agent gives the correct answer on the four highest-cost questions, refund clocks and change fees, accessibility by vessel, shuttle eligibility and dietary windows, in their first week on the phone, with the published sentence and its page in front of them.
Every answer the tool gives carries its own source, and any input combination with no published rule behind it escalates to a named role by design rather than being interpolated or guessed.

Major Marine ends the engagement holding three assets it keeps whether or not another line of software is ever written: one canonical dated policy source, an authoritative vessel-to-departure map, and a written record of what your desk actually gets asked.
A recorded baseline exists where none exists today, so the next decision, including a decision to spend nothing further, is made on counted evidence rather than on anybody's impression.
The question of whether a tool with a model in it is ever worth building at this desk is settled by a threshold agreed in writing in advance that is capable of returning no.

non_goals.item: Nothing in phase one faces a guest. No website chatbot, no widget, no automated reply, no guest-visible answer of any kind.
non_goals.reason: A guest-facing answering tool puts confident wrong answers on the guest side of a thirty year locally owned reputation before any record exists of how often it would be confidently wrong. That reputation is your defence against a NYSE-listed operator in the same harbour, and it is not something to spend on an unmeasured tool. This is deferred and gated, not dead.

non_goals.item: No model, no generated wording, no paraphrase anywhere on the four high-cost branches.
non_goals.reason: Those four have a finite input space, answers you have already published, and the highest cost when they are wrong. A deterministic table can be tested against every possible input and certified rather than sampled. A model would answer a little more smoothly and a little less reliably, and on the 8:00 a.m. shuttle exclusion a little less reliably means a guest walks to the harbour for a sailing they will miss. This is enforced as a topic filter in code, not as an instruction anybody can override.

non_goals.item: No integration with your booking system in phase one. The agent types in what the booking contains.
non_goals.reason: We can't identify your booking engine from the outside and we refuse to guess at it, so we can't scope that integration honestly. Saying so keeps the estimate real instead of hiding unscoped work inside it. If phase one earns a second stage, the integration gets scoped properly with your vendor in the room.

non_goals.item: No voice agent on the reservations line, at any price, in any phase.
non_goals.reason: That line is a revenue channel, not a support queue. Packages are bookable by phone only, all discounts must be booked directly with you, and within 12 hours of departure your own reservation page tells the guest to call. Placing a machine in front of purchase intent risks revenue to save labour, which inverts the business case. The callers who most need a person, the ones already in trouble, are also the ones a bot meets first.

non_goals.item: No change to phone-only packages and no self-serve package builder.
non_goals.reason: Phone-only sits directly next to a published direct-only discount rule and a named Director of Sales, which is at least as consistent with a deliberate margin and upsell decision as with a gap. Proposing to remove a revenue mechanism while calling it a fix would be us guessing at your sales strategy. If it is deliberate, we have scoped nothing against it, which is the right outcome.

non_goals.item: No change to your check-in rule or the rail connection.
non_goals.reason: You already handle it. Your check-in page footnotes the train case explicitly, so the on-time rail arrival is a solved problem and we treat it as one. The only piece that stays a human judgement call is the late train, which your FAQ describes as a best-effort transfer to a different date or the 12:30 p.m. 4 Hour cruise. Discretion is the right design there and we are leaving it alone.

non_goals.item: No self-serve cancellation for guests.
non_goals.reason: This is a field-wide gap rather than anything specific to you, so building it here would be solving a category problem on your budget while your competitors carry the same one. It is not in scope and we would not price it.

non_goals.item: No model drafting disruption notices, and no seat-allocation optimiser.
non_goals.reason: On disruption notices your goal is that the message is identical every time, and a template with merge fields is identical by construction while a model is identical only under supervision, so a model is worse on the actual objective. On seat allocation there is no evidence at all that staff assigning seats before a cruise causes anybody a problem, and building on speculation is how a project ends with nothing to measure.

non_goals.item: No website redesign, and website tidiness is not the product.
non_goals.reason: The reconciliation work in phase one is content operations, deciding which of two published statements is the correct one and giving it one dated home. Your site is not the deliverable and we are not pitching one. This is ordinary housekeeping that any site of this age accumulates, and it is cheap to settle.

non_goals.item: No review-response tooling, and we would talk you out of buying it elsewhere.
non_goals.reason: An audit of 61,459 model calls across 12 models measured responding to reviews at +0.1 percentage points on how likely a model is to recommend a business, which is statistically indistinguishable from zero, against about +32 points for guest rating. That measures how models recommend rather than what human readers think, so it does not prove replies are worthless to people. In the channel that tooling is currently sold on, it buys nothing measurable. That finding is yours with no invoice attached.

success_metrics.metric: A recorded baseline for the reservations desk exists at all. Question asked, time to answer, escalated or not, and to whom, one line per question, on paper.
success_metrics.baseline: ZERO. There is no baseline today and we are not inventing one. Median time to answer, escalation rate and misquote count are recorded nowhere at Major Marine that we can find, and nothing in this document assumes a starting number for any of them. The baseline is a deliverable of this engagement, not an assumption inside it.
success_metrics.target: At least 30 complete operating days of tally sheets between sign-off and October 11th, 2026, including at least 10 days after September 21st when the 4 Hour is the only cruise still running, plus at least 4 full days logged by a supervisor on randomly chosen dates.
success_metrics.timeframe: Starts within two weeks of sign-off, ends October 11th, 2026. Every week of delay costs a week of baseline that can't be recovered until the 2027 season.
success_metrics.how_measured: Paper on the desk. Zero software and zero cost. The supervisor-logged days exist to correct the sheet's own bias, since under-logging is guaranteed at peak and peak is exactly when errors happen.
success_metrics.falsifiable_how: It fails if fewer than 30 complete days come back, and we would report that plainly rather than analyse a partial sheet as though it were a season.

success_metrics.metric: The decision table agrees with your published policy on every possible input, and never answers without showing its source.
success_metrics.baseline: No enumeration of these rules exists today and there is no single signed-off source. The four branches currently live across your refund policy page, your FAQ and your Seward check-in page.
success_metrics.target: 100 percent agreement across an exhaustive enumeration of the input cross product, not a sample, signed off by your named policy owner before the tool ships. Plus zero responses of any kind that lack the verbatim published sentence and its source URL, checked as an assertion on every single response.
success_metrics.timeframe: Certified before March 7th, 2027, and re-run as a regression suite on every content change and before March 7th of each following season.
success_metrics.how_measured: The signed cell table is itself the test. This is the one component in the whole proposal whose acceptance bar can be certified rather than sampled, which is a direct consequence of keeping a model out of it.
success_metrics.falsifiable_how: One disagreeing cell fails it. There is no threshold to hide behind.

success_metrics.metric: Conflicting or stale statements between your own published pages, resolved into one canonical dated source.
success_metrics.baseline: FOUR, found in one afternoon of outside reading and verified. Two published statements about parking price that don't agree, $10 per vehicle per day in one place and $15 for the day at the kiosk in another. A live 2026 booking page still carrying a line about a departure being new in 2021 and not available in 2020. A vessel named in the FAQ as running the 12:30 p.m. 4 Hour departure that is not on the eight-vessel fleet page, which we could not resolve from outside and are not asserting either way. A cruise with a live 2026 product page that is missing from the all-cruises index, which lists five.
success_metrics.target: Zero unresolved conflicts in the canonical source. Each of the four adjudicated by your named policy owner with a date against the decision, plus a re-crawl showing zero before the season opens.
success_metrics.timeframe: Canonical source dated and signed by January 31st, 2027, re-crawled before March 7th, 2027 and before each season after that.
success_metrics.how_measured: A crawl and a diff over roughly thirty pages. This is ordinary for a site of this age and cheap to settle, and it is worth doing whether or not a line of software ever gets written, since it improves the website, both hotel front desks and the dock on a day nothing has been installed anywhere.
success_metrics.falsifiable_how: The re-crawl either returns zero conflicts or it does not.

success_metrics.metric: First-season desk outcomes on the four branches, measured like for like against the recorded 2026 baseline.
success_metrics.baseline: Not yet known, and knowable only after metric 1 runs. Whatever the 2026 tally records for August 10th to October 11th is the baseline, and we will publish the figure it produces before we compare anything to it.
success_metrics.target: Median time to answer on the four branches down at least 40 percent. Escalations where the answer was already published on your own pages down at least half. Zero policy misquotes on the four branches across the supervisor-sampled days. All three, with no fall in whatever guest-experience measure you already keep.
success_metrics.timeframe: Measured August 10th to October 11th, 2027, the same calendar weeks as the baseline, reported by November 2027.
success_metrics.how_measured: The same tally sheet, run again in the same weeks. Escalations that the design intends, meaning no published rule exists or the vessel serving a departure is not known with certainty, are counted separately and are never scored as failures, because routing those to a person is the tool working correctly.
success_metrics.note: One honest limitation, stated here rather than discovered later. A late-season tally gives a clean like-for-like comparison and it does NOT give a baseline for the March to May ramp, because that ramp happened in spring 2026 before anybody was counting and can't be reconstructed. So the ramp figure can only be measured forward, starting March 2027, and in 2027 it is reported as a level rather than as an improvement. Its first honest comparison year is 2028. The 40 percent and the half are targets we chose and committed to. Neither is derived from any published study, and no outside percentage is attached to your desk anywhere in this document.
success_metrics.falsifiable_how: Three numbers against three recorded numbers in the same weeks. If they miss, we say they missed, in the same document that carried the target.

must: THE PAPER TALLY SHEET, STARTING NOW. One line per question at the desk: what was asked, how long the answer took, whether it was escalated, and to whom. Zero software and zero cost. It does three jobs at once, it creates the baseline that does not exist, it counts how often weather re-routes and late trains actually happen so nobody builds a disruption tool on a guess, and it starts the record of what your desk gets asked before any tool exists. Plus two randomly chosen full days a month logged by a supervisor, to correct the sheet's own under-logging at peak.

CORPUS RECONCILIATION TO ONE CANONICAL DATED SOURCE. A crawl of roughly thirty pages that finds every statement that conflicts with another, your named owner adjudicating each one because only you know which parking price is right, then one canonical versioned source with a date on it and a review trigger, at minimum before March 7th each season and after any price or schedule change. Season scoping is part of the specification rather than a refinement, because two seasons are live at once on your pages today.

THE AUTHORITATIVE VESSEL-TO-DEPARTURE MAP. Which vessel runs which departure, in one place, with a named owner and a date. Nothing public provides this, and the FAQ against fleet page disagreement is direct evidence that internally it lives in more than one place and the copies differ. Every accessibility, seating and capacity answer depends on it. If it turns out assignment moves with maintenance and charters and can't be pinned, the honest design is that the tool never answers accessibility and always routes it to a named person, and we would agree that up front rather than discover it mid-build.

THE DECISION TABLE over the four highest-cost branches, refund clocks and change fees, accessibility by vessel, shuttle eligibility, and dietary windows. The agent enters four or five structured facts and gets back a date, a fee, an eligibility, and the verbatim published sentence to read out loud with its page. Default deny: any combination with no published rule behind it returns escalate to the named role and writes a log entry. It never interpolates and it never guesses. Accessibility additionally abstains whenever the vessel serving that departure is not known with certainty. Standalone, with booking contents entered by hand.

THE MISS LOG, SPECIFIED PROPERLY. Questions captured verbatim rather than as a category tick, every entry carrying a labelled correct answer from a named internal authority with its source page, a held-out portion never looked at during development, deliberately constructed out-of-scope cases the system should refuse, the supervisor sampling arm above, re-labelling each season, and a written rule about what gets redacted at capture and who may read it, agreed before the first entry. It is your data in your format, portable. You can take it to any vendor, including one that is not us, or to nobody.
later_explicitly_not_in_phase_one: THE SNIPPET SEARCH OPTION. Staff-facing search over the reconciled source that returns the verbatim published sentence and its page, never composed prose, with the four high-cost branches filtered to the table in code before search ever runs. This is written down and priced now, and it is NOT sold now. It is gated on a number that can fail: at least 15 percent of logged desk questions falling outside the table, AND at least 20 distinct question types recurring three or more times, AND at least 150 labelled items after de-duplication. Those figures are ours to propose and yours to set. What is not negotiable is that a number exists and that it can return no. If the log lands below it, we say so in writing, we do not invoice, and the published conclusion is that this business needed a rule set and not an AI.

The honest date for that option is the March 2028 cohort, not 2027. The questions that would justify it can only be collected while a season runs, so collection is roughly March to October 2027, labelling and building over that winter, and the desk sees it in spring 2028. Anyone showing you both against one March 2027 date is compressing two seasons into one.
Running the same tally in the first six weeks of the 2027 season, to create the ramp baseline that can't be reconstructed for 2026.

A guest-facing answering tool, gated on a full season of internal evidence, and if ever built, running on a whitelist that never answers a refund, accessibility or shuttle question, with escalate-to-a-person as the default.

Disruption handling as a batch of the same entitlement logic, gated on the event count the tally sheet produces. Your own pages say cruises go out rain or shine and are cancelled only for unsafe sea conditions, so the frequency may be too low to justify anything, and that is worth knowing before it is built.
The package configurator, gated on a conversation about whether phone-only is a deliberate sales decision.
Seat allocation, gated on any evidence at all that the current process hurts anybody.

phase1_must: The paper tally sheet at the desk, starting within two weeks of sign-off and running to October 11th, 2026, plus two supervisor-logged full days a month.
Corpus reconciliation of roughly thirty pages into one canonical, dated, owned policy source, with season scoping built in and a review trigger before March 7th each year.
The authoritative vessel-to-departure map, with a named owner, a date, and an agreed abstain route if the assignment turns out not to be stable.

The deterministic decision table over refund clocks and change fees, accessibility by vessel, shuttle eligibility and dietary windows, returning the verbatim published sentence and its page, default deny on anything not in the table, standalone with manual entry of booking contents.

The properly specified miss log, with labelled answers from a named internal authority, a held-out split, deliberate out-of-scope cases, the supervisor sampling arm, seasonal re-labelling and a PII rule agreed before the first entry.
phase1_later: Staff-facing snippet search over the reconciled source, priced now, not sold now, gated on 15 percent of logged questions outside the table AND 20 recurring question types AND 150 labelled items, with the figures yours to set, and a 2028 date rather than 2027.
Re-running the tally in the first six weeks of the 2027 season to build the ramp baseline that 2026 can't provide.
A guest-facing answering tool, gated on a full season of internal evidence, whitelist only, never answering refunds, accessibility or shuttle eligibility.
Disruption handling as a batch, gated on the event frequency the tally sheet counts.
The package configurator, gated on whether phone-only bookings are a deliberate sales decision.
Seat allocation, gated on any evidence that the present process causes a problem.
prd.commercial_shape: Phase one is a fixed price of $18,000, covering roughly one person-month to build and exhaustively test the decision table, about half a month of content operations on reconciliation and facilitating the vessel map, and the miss log tooling. The snippet search option is priced separately and is not part of this number. It is invoiced only if the gate clears on your figures, and if it fails we publish that result rather than bury it. We will say the uncomfortable part plainly: a meaningful share of what you are buying in phase one is decision data and three assets you keep, rather than hours saved. Absolute hours saved here are modest, because the desk is small and its headcount is not something we can see from outside. This is a ramp-time and error-rate case that recurs every spring, and the price is sized to match that and nothing larger.
what_we_need_from_you: ONE PERSON TO RUN THE PAPER TALLY FOR NINE WEEKS, named, starting within two weeks of sign-off and running to October 11th, 2026. This is the single heaviest thing we are asking for and it is the one we can't substitute for. If nobody at Major Marine will run it, the outcome of this project is unmeasurable, and we would say so in writing rather than promise you a measured improvement. An unmeasurable claim is not a smaller claim, it is a different kind of claim.

A NAMED INTERNAL POLICY OWNER with the authority to decide, not just to advise. The concrete first test is which of your two published parking prices is correct, $10 per vehicle per day or $15 for the day at the kiosk. Only somebody inside Major Marine can settle that, and there will be a short queue of similar calls behind it. Budget a few hours across a few weeks, not a project role.

A NAMED OWNER FOR THE VESSEL-TO-DEPARTURE MAP, with a date. This data does not exist in verified published form and, on the evidence, may not sit in one place internally either. If it turns out that assignment moves with maintenance and charters and can't be pinned to a departure reliably, tell us that early and we will ship accessibility as always-abstain. That is a smaller tool, and we would rather scope it that way in writing than discover it in build.

SIGN-OFF ON THE ENUMERATED CELL TABLE BEFORE THE TOOL SHIPS. Every cell, carrying the published answer, signed by your policy owner. That signature is the acceptance test for the whole build. It is your signature rather than ours by design, because we should not be the ones certifying what your policy says.

AGREEMENT IN WRITING, BEFORE PHASE ONE STARTS, ON TWO THINGS. The boundaries of the decision table, meaning what counts as inside it and what counts as a miss. The numeric gate on the search option. Both belong to you rather than to us, and here is the reason we are being blunt about it: a narrower table produces a fatter miss log, and we are the party that designs the table. That conflict is structural, so it gets disclosed and neutralised up front rather than left in the room.

A PII DECISION BEFORE THE FIRST LOG ENTRY. The log captures guest questions verbatim, which means names, booking references, mobility details and dietary details. Mobility and dietary information is health adjacent. We need your rule on what gets redacted at capture, how long entries are kept, and who may read them, agreed before anybody writes line one.
SUPERVISOR TIME FOR TWO RANDOMLY CHOSEN FULL DAYS A MONTH during the tally. The sheet under-records at peak, which is exactly when errors happen, and this is the cheap correction for that bias.

A LABELLING BUDGET WITH A NAME AGAINST IT, only if the search option is ever exercised. Roughly 150 to 300 real questions, each given a correct answer and a source page by somebody internal who actually knows. It has to be your people rather than us and rather than a model. This is real hours from people who are busy, and if it is refused, the honest response is that the log is a backlog, the option is unfundable on that evidence, and we say so.

ONE DECISION-MAKER AND A SIGN-OFF DATE no later than mid-February 2027. Phase one has to be in the March cohort's hands before March 7th. If sign-off slips past that, we will tell you it slipped and re-plan for 2028 rather than push a half-tested tool into a season that has already started.

ACCESS TO ANY INTERNAL POLICY SOURCE THAT DIFFERS FROM YOUR PUBLIC PAGES. That is the whole access list. Phase one needs no system credentials, no booking system access, no guest data and no network access of any kind.

risks.risk: Nobody runs the tally sheet, or it runs for two weeks and stops. This is the most likely way this project disappoints you, and it is a dependency on your side rather than ours.
risks.mitigation: We designed it to be paper, one line, no software and no login, precisely because a tool nobody has time to open is not a measurement. If it runs partially, we report the partial and we don't analyse nine days as though they were a season. If it doesn't run at all, metrics 2 and 3 still stand on their own, since they don't depend on it, the outcome metric goes unproven, and we publish that it went unproven rather than replacing it with a modelled number.

risks.risk: The desk may simply be too small for any of this to matter. Your reservations headcount and your question volume are not published anywhere we can see, so nobody outside Major Marine knows whether the prize here is worth $18,000.
risks.mitigation: That is exactly what nine weeks of paper answers, at zero cost, before the build starts. If the tally shows a desk that rarely escalates and rarely stalls, that is a real finding and the correct response is to stop, and we would say so. We would rather find that in September than in March. This risk is also why the ask is sized at $18,000 and not at three times that.

risks.risk: The vessel-to-departure map may not be stable, or may not be reconstructable at all. The accessibility branch is the highest-value part of the table and it depends entirely on that map.
risks.mitigation: The abstain route is designed in from the start rather than added as a patch. Where the vessel serving a departure is not known with certainty, the tool refuses to answer and routes to a named person, and it says why. If that turns out to be the permanent state, you get a smaller tool for the same rigour, and we would put that in writing during week one rather than at delivery.

risks.risk: The search option's gate might fail, and the party proposing the gate is the party that benefits from clearing it.
risks.mitigation: The threshold is numeric, agreed in advance, and capable of returning no, which is the only kind of gate worth having. The boundaries of the table are yours to set, so the definition of a miss is not ours to adjust after the fact. If the number lands short, we don't invoice and we publish the conclusion that this business needed a rule set rather than an AI. Phase one is deliberately built to be worth buying on its own with no obligation to a second stage.

risks.risk: The table drifts out of date. Prices change, schedules change, a vessel moves, and a tool confidently reads out last season's sentence.
risks.mitigation: Two named dependencies, both checkable by inspection rather than by sampling: whether the encoded rules match the published policy on the day, and whether the vessel map is current. The regression suite re-runs on every content change and before March 7th each season, and season scoping of every dated and priced fact is enforced in code because two seasons are live at once on your site today.

risks.risk: Adoption on a phone desk is harder than it looks. An agent has to read a screen while a guest waits, which is a different situation from the office settings where tools like this have been measured.
risks.mitigation: Four or five structured inputs on one screen, and the output is a date, a fee, an eligibility and the sentence to read out loud. We test it with an actual first-season agent in their first hour, not with a veteran who already knows the answer, because a veteran passing the test proves nothing about the person it was built for.

risks.risk: The measurement will run across a handful of people over a few weeks, where individual variation is large. A small sample can show noise that reads like failure, or noise that flatters us.
risks.mitigation: We pre-commit to how the result will be read before we see any data, we report per-person figures and the spread alongside the pooled number rather than only a median, and we compare the same calendar weeks. If the result is inside the noise, the honest report says the result is inside the noise.

risks.risk: We may have picked the wrong four branches. Our ranking of what costs the most came from reading your published policies from the outside, not from your desk.
risks.mitigation: The tally can overturn it, and it runs before a line of the table is written. If the counted questions say the expensive ones are somewhere else, we re-cut the table before build and we tell you our ranking was wrong.

risks.risk: It underperforms. The tool ships, it is correct on every cell, and the 2027 numbers move less than the targets above.
risks.mitigation: Here is what happens, written down now rather than negotiated then. We report the miss against the same targets in the same document that carried them. We do not re-baseline after the fact and we do not quietly swap in a metric that did move. You keep the canonical policy source, the vessel map and the record of what your desk gets asked, which are yours regardless, and the honest recommendation in that case is to stop rather than to buy a bigger version of something that did not work.

open_questions.q: How many people work the reservations desk in season, and how many questions does it handle in a day? This is the biggest unknown in the whole proposal, it is unpublished, and it decides whether any of this is worth doing. Every hours-saved figure before it is answered would be an invented denominator, so we have not written one.
open_questions.owner: Major Marine, answered by the tally sheet rather than by an estimate. Colby Lawrence or the Director of Shoreside Operations to nominate the person who runs it.

open_questions.q: Which parking price is correct, $10 per vehicle per day or $15 for the day at the kiosk?
open_questions.owner: The named internal policy owner. First adjudication, and the template for the rest.

open_questions.q: Does vessel-to-departure assignment stay fixed across a season, or does it move with maintenance and charters? The answer decides whether accessibility ships as an answer or ships as an abstain.
open_questions.owner: Major Marine, most likely the Port Captain and the Operations Manager together.

open_questions.q: The vessel named in your FAQ as running the 12:30 p.m. 4 Hour departure is not on the fleet page. Is it chartered, retired, or simply not listed? We could not resolve this from outside and we are not asserting either way.
open_questions.owner: Major Marine. It matters because the 4 Hour is the product that runs latest in the season.

open_questions.q: Is packages-by-phone-only a deliberate sales decision? We are assuming it is, and we have scoped nothing against it on that assumption.
open_questions.owner: Kori Goertz, Director of Sales. One conversation, and it either closes a Later item or opens it.

open_questions.q: Who may read the miss log, what gets redacted at capture, and how long are entries kept?
open_questions.owner: Major Marine, owner or Vice President, decided before the first entry is written.

open_questions.q: What are the final figures on the search option's gate? We propose 15 percent outside the table, 20 recurring question types, and 150 labelled items. The numbers are yours to set. What is not negotiable is that a number exists and that it can fail.
open_questions.owner: Joint, in writing, before phase one starts.

open_questions.q: How often does a weather re-route into Resurrection Bay happen, and how often does a late train force a manual transfer? Your pages say cruises go out rain or shine and are cancelled only for unsafe sea conditions, so the count may be small enough to close a Later item permanently.
open_questions.owner: The tally sheet, which counts both at zero extra cost.

open_questions.q: Does an internal policy source already exist that differs from your public pages? If it does, it is the real canonical source and the reconciliation starts from it rather than from the website.
open_questions.owner: Major Marine, in the first week.

prd.the_next_step: Start the tally sheet. It costs nothing, it needs no decision about us, and it is the one thing on this list that expires. There are roughly nine weeks left in the 2026 season. If you want, we will send the one-page sheet and the four column headings, and you can run it whether or not you ever hire us.
prd.constraint_compliance_note: Every pain claim in this document rests on Major Marine's own published policies rather than on any guest saying anything. Nothing here implies a guest complained or was dissatisfied, and no guest review is cited anywhere. No outside percentage is attached to a Major Marine metric. The booking engine vendor is never named or guessed. The check-in rule is treated as handled, with only the late train left as a manual judgement call, which we recommend leaving manual. Website conflicts appear only as evidence for corpus readiness, framed as ordinary and cheap to settle, and never as a headline finding. There is no baseline number invented anywhere, the baseline is a deliverable and is labelled as one in every metric that depends on it.

design.one_liner: Build a staff-only lookup for the Major Marine reservations desk that answers refund clocks and change fees, accessibility by vessel, shuttle eligibility and dietary windows from a dated, season scoped copy of the company's own published sentences, with no model anywhere in the funded scope, so a March 2027 hire gets the right answer and the exact sentence to read out loud in their first hour on the desk.
design.outcome_it_moves: A first-season agent answers the four highest cost of error questions correctly and unaided, and every answer they give is traceable to a published sentence with its URL. Measured against the paper tally baseline started in the final nine weeks of the 2026 season and re-measured in the same calendar weeks of 2027.

components.name: Desk Tally Sheet
components.tech: A printed one page grid on a clipboard at the reservations desk. One row per question. Columns are time, topic code, minutes to answer, escalated yes or no, to whom, and a free box for the question as asked.
components.responsibility: Create the baseline that does not exist today. Median time to answer, escalation rate and misquote count are recorded nowhere (feasibility.data_readiness.baseline_data). It also counts weather re-route and cancellation events for the whole season, which is the denominator the disruption console would need, and it starts the miss log before any tool exists.
components.starts: The week of August 10th 2026. Nine weeks of the 2026 season remain, the season ends October 11th 2026 (c27).
components.writes: Paper. Transcribed weekly into misslog_db by a named supervisor.
components.owner: A named Major Marine supervisor. We propose the Operations Manager or the Director of Shoreside Operations, both named on their published team page, and they choose.
components.pii_rule: No guest names, no booking references and no phone numbers on paper, topic codes and tally marks only. Sheets are shredded after transcription.

components.name: Policy Canon Workbook
components.tech: One spreadsheet workbook in whatever office suite Major Marine already runs, exported to CSV and committed to the repo. No live spreadsheet API in phase one, deliberately, so there is no OAuth dependency and no vendor to name.
components.responsibility: The adjudication surface where a named internal policy owner decides which of two conflicting published statements is the true one. Four conflicts are already found from one afternoon of external reading, two different parking prices on their own pages (c36), 2020 and 2021 copy on a live 2026 booking page (c37), a vessel named in the FAQ running the 12:30 pm departure that the eight vessel fleet page does not list (c21), and a live 2026 product page for the Orca Quest Cruise that the five product all-cruises index omits.
components.required_columns: rule_id, branch, input_key, verbatim_sentence, source_url, season, effective_from, effective_to, adjudicated_by, adjudicated_on, status. A row with an empty verbatim_sentence or an empty source_url fails the build.
components.writes: The named internal policy owner writes. Nobody else.
components.build_or_buy: buy the spreadsheet, build the schema

components.name: Vessel to Departure Map
components.tech: vessel_map.csv in the same repo. Keyed by season, product, departure_time, effective_from, effective_to. Value is a fleet vessel name or the literal UNKNOWN.
components.responsibility: The single authoritative answer to which boat runs which departure. Every accessibility answer depends on it, because accessibility differs vessel by vessel and no vessel takes a motorized wheelchair (c20). This data does not exist in verified published form and the FAQ versus fleet page disagreement is direct evidence that internally it lives in more than one place and the copies disagree (c21).
components.unknown_is_first_class: UNKNOWN is a value, not a missing row. An UNKNOWN or an expired effective_to forces the accessibility branch to abstain and route to a named human. Abstention is the correct answer here, not a failure.
components.writes: A named Major Marine operations owner, by a named date agreed at kickoff. The accessibility branch does not ship without both.
components.build_or_buy: build, because it does not exist anywhere to be bought or copied

components.name: canon-build
components.tech: Python 3.12, pydantic for the schema, click for the CLI. Runs locally and in GitHub Actions.
components.responsibility: Compile canon_workbook plus vessel_map into canon.json, a signed, versioned, dated bundle. Hard fails on a missing verbatim sentence, a missing source URL, a missing season on any dated or priced fact, an overlapping effective range inside one input key, or a vessel map row whose effective_to has passed.
components.enforces: Two of the three conscience requirements at build time. No fact enters the canon without its verbatim sentence and URL. No dated or priced fact enters without a season.
components.writes: canon.json, plus canon_version and certified_on stamps.

components.name: deskanswer-core, the decision table
components.tech: TypeScript, compiled to the browser bundle and also runnable in Node for the certification suite. Pure and side effect free. Signature is answer(branch, inputs, canon) which returns Answer or Abstain and nothing else.
components.responsibility: The four branches. Refund clocks and change fees, accessibility by vessel, shuttle eligibility, dietary windows. It resolves a cell in a finite enumerated table and returns the published sentence for the agent to read aloud.

branches.inputs: booking contents (cruise only, cruise plus hotel package, motorcoach or train added), days before departure, count of prior date changes, no-show flag, weather re-route flag
branches.grounded_in: 72 hours cruise only (c4), 7 days hotel package (c6), 21 days transportation (c7), 3 percent card fee retained (c5), one free change up to 24 hours then a fee per person (c8, two sentences, never spliced), no-show completely non-refundable (c9, never spliced next to the clocks), Resurrection Bay partial refund at the Captain's discretion (c10)

branches.inputs: departure date, product, departure time, mobility type from a fixed vocabulary
branches.grounded_in: c20, accessible on first deck inside the main cabin only, outside decks not accessible, no vessel takes a motorized wheelchair
branches.special_rule: Resolves the vessel through vessel_map first. UNKNOWN or expired means abstain, always, with no fallback and no interpolation.

branches.inputs: product and departure time, hours of notice, advance reservation made yes or no, pickup point
branches.grounded_in: call at least 24 hours before (c13, full sentence), advance reservations required and not available for the 8:00 am 6 Hour cruise (c14), terminal loop 7:00 am to 9:45 am every 15 minutes (c15), 0.6 miles from Harbor 360 and 0.8 miles from the South Harbor office (c16), all cruises board at the Harbor 360 Hotel office (c17)

branches.inputs: product, request timing relative to the reservation
branches.grounded_in: vegetarian sandwich requestable in advance at the time of reservation on the 6 Hour, 7.5 Hour and 8.5 Hour cruises (c19), the 4 Hour has no meal and a snack bar onboard

components.default_deny: Any input combination not in the table returns 'no published rule for this case, escalate to <named role>' and writes a miss log row. It never interpolates and never guesses.
components.season_rule: Season is never inferred. The form requires a departure DATE and the engine resolves the season from that date against effective_from and effective_to. Where one question has two correct answers in two live seasons the engine returns BOTH, each labelled with its season, rather than choosing. The 4 Hour Kenai Fjords Wildlife Cruise is 149 dollars for 2026 while the 4 Hour Spring Wildlife Cruise is already published at 109 dollars for March 20th to May 16th 2027, so 'what does the 4 Hour cost' has two correct answers today. With no date supplied the engine abstains.
components.assertion: assert(answer.verbatim_sentence && answer.source_url && answer.season) runs on every returned Answer, in the library, not in a prompt. A response that fails the assertion throws rather than degrading to a partial answer.

components.name: redlist-router
components.tech: TypeScript, sits in front of decision_engine and in front of a RetrieverPort interface that has exactly one implementation in phase one, NullRetriever, which throws if it is ever called.
components.responsibility: Route refunds and change fees, accessibility, shuttle eligibility and dietary questions to the decision table BEFORE any retriever runs. In phase one there is no retriever, so this component exists to make it structurally impossible to wire one in later without going through the filter.
components.why_it_ships_in_phase_one_with_nothing_b: The conscience gate requires the filter in code and not in a prompt. Adding it after a retriever exists means adding it to a system that already works without it, which is the moment it gets skipped. It ships first and empty, with a contract test.
components.contract_test: test_redlist_never_reaches_retriever.ts registers a spy retriever, replays every red list branch across the full enumerated input set, and asserts the spy call count is exactly zero. The test runs on every commit and is a required check on the repo.

components.name: Desk Answer, the agent lookup
components.kind: static single page app, offline capable
components.tech: TypeScript and Preact, no backend on the answer path. canon.json is inlined into the bundle at build time. Served from Cloudflare Pages, installed as a PWA with a service worker so the desk keeps answering with no network.
components.responsibility: One form per branch, four or five structured fields, no free text on the answer path at all. The answer card renders the verbatim published sentence as the largest element on the screen with the words 'read this to the guest', the source URL under it, the season label, the canon version and the certified date. The inputs are echoed back on the card so a wrong entry is visible before it is spoken.
components.no_paraphrase_by_construction: There is no free text field in the render path and no string concatenation of policy language. A contract test asserts the answer card component receives only canon-sourced strings.
components.manual_booking_entry: The booking engine vendor is unidentified and is never named or guessed, so phase one is a STANDALONE tool. The agent reads the booking contents off their existing screen and enters the three discriminating facts by hand, does the booking include motorcoach or train, does it include a hotel night, how many prior date changes. Each field carries the published sentence that makes it matter, next to the field. This is a real limitation, stated rather than hidden, and it is the price of refusing to scope an integration against a vendor nobody has verified.
components.writes: misslog_api, async, fire and forget with a local queue.
components.build_or_buy: build the app, buy the hosting

components.name: misslog-api
components.tech: Cloudflare Worker, TypeScript, behind Cloudflare Access. Three routes, POST /miss, POST /telemetry, GET /supervisor-data.
components.responsibility: Accept miss log rows and telemetry, run the server side redaction second pass, reject anything that still matches an identifier pattern, and write to misslog_db.
components.build_or_buy: build the Worker, buy the runtime

components.name: Miss Log
components.tech: Neon Postgres, US region pinned, TLS only, credentials held as Worker secrets.
components.schema: id, created_at, branch, structured_inputs jsonb, outcome (answered, abstained, no_rule), question_text_redacted, agent_pseudonym (a hash of the Cloudflare Access subject, never a name), sampling_day boolean, label_correct_answer, label_source_url, label_author_role, label_added_on, holdout boolean, out_of_corpus boolean. There is NO name column, NO booking reference column and NO free text column other than question_text_redacted.
components.responsibility: The eval set that decides whether retrieval is ever discussed, and the record of what the desk actually gets asked. It is THEIR data in THEIR format, exportable to CSV on demand, portable to any vendor including one that is not us.
components.build_or_buy: build the schema, buy the database

components.name: canon-certify
components.tech: Vitest in GitHub Actions. Enumerates the FULL input cross product of all four branches, estimated at 300 to 900 cells once branch boundaries are agreed, and asserts 100 percent agreement with the signed off cell table.
components.responsibility: The acceptance bar, and it is a specification rather than a sampled eval set. This is the one component in the whole proposal whose bar can be certified rather than estimated. It runs on every canon commit, before ship, and on a scheduled workflow every February so it is green before March 7th, the season opening date (c27).
components.also_asserts: Every returned Answer carries a verbatim sentence, a source URL and a season. Every red list branch reaches the table with zero retriever calls. Two live seasons return two answers rather than one.
components.writes: A pass or fail, a certified_on stamp, and a signed cell table artefact.
components.reads: canon.json, the signed off cell table.

components.name: canon-drift
components.tech: Python, httpx and selectolax, GitHub Actions on a weekly cron. Roughly thirty pages on majormarine.com, plain HTML, owned outright, no PII.
components.responsibility: Fetch every source URL in the canon and diff the live page against the stored verbatim sentence. Any mismatch opens a GitHub issue naming the rule, the branch and the two strings.
components.teeth: A drift hit on a red list branch sets branch_status to ABSTAIN for that branch automatically until a human adjudicates it. The tool degrades to 'ask a person' rather than to a stale answer.
components.writes: GitHub issues, and branch_status in the canon.
components.build_or_buy: build, and it is plumbing, never sold as an AI website checker

components.name: Supervisor view
components.tech: Same SPA, a route locked to two named roles by a Cloudflare Access policy.
components.responsibility: Show the gate counters live, computed from their own log rather than by us at the end. Percent of logged questions falling outside the table, count of distinct question types recurring three or more times, count of labelled items after de-duplication, abstain rate by branch, and the two supervisor sampling days scheduled for the month.
components.why_it_matters: The party who benefits from clearing the retrieval gate is the party who designs the table that determines what counts as a miss. Putting the counters on a page the client watches all season, computed from their data, is the structural fix for that conflict of interest.

components.name: Printed fallback card
components.tech: One laminated double sided sheet, regenerated by canon-build on every certification.
components.responsibility: The four branches at their most common inputs, with the verbatim sentences, for the case where the login provider is down or the desk has no network and no cached app. It carries the same canon version stamp as the app so a stale card is visible.

cross_cutting.auth: Cloudflare Access in front of everything, staff only, no public route to any surface, no guest facing surface at all. Two Access groups, desk_agent and desk_supervisor. The supervisor route and the miss log read are locked to desk_supervisor, which is two named people. Access logs give a per person record of who opened what, which is the audit trail the miss log needs and which we would otherwise have had to build. Seasonal provisioning matches their published hiring window, adds in January and February, removals at contract end. There is no password to leak, no session store of ours, and no account that survives a season by accident.
cross_cutting.data_security: The miss log is the only place personal data lands, and it will otherwise capture guest names, booking references, mobility information and dietary information, which is health adjacent. Four structural controls, agreed in writing BEFORE the first entry. ONE, there is no name column, no booking reference column, and the only free text column is question_text_redacted. TWO, redaction happens at capture in the browser, before the payload leaves the desk. scrub.ts strips digit runs of four or more, email patterns, and anything matching their booking reference shape, and the Worker runs a second pass and rejects a row that still matches rather than storing it. THREE, mobility and dietary facts are captured as coded values from a fixed vocabulary, never as free prose attached to a person, and the agent identifier is a hash of the Access subject rather than a name. FOUR, retention is 400 days on a scheduled delete job, which is one season plus the labelling winter and then gone, and read access is two named roles. The paper tally has its own rule, topic codes and tally marks only, no guest names, shredded after transcription. One property is worth stating plainly. No model runs anywhere in the funded scope, so no guest question, no mobility fact and no dietary fact is ever sent to a model vendor, because there is no model vendor. Data residency is US on both Cloudflare and Neon. The whole log exports to CSV on one command and it is theirs.
cross_cutting.observability: Certification is the primary signal and it is binary. canon-certify runs on every canon commit and on a February cron, and the app footer shows canon_version and certified_on on every single answer card, so a stale canon is visible to the agent rather than to a dashboard nobody opens. If the bundle in the browser is older than the last certified canon the app shows a banner. Runtime telemetry is branch, answered or abstained, canon_version and client side lookup latency, with no free text and no guest data. Abstain rate by branch is the health metric that matters most, because a rising abstain rate on accessibility means the vessel map has gone stale. canon-drift reports weekly against the live site. The four retrieval gate counters render on the supervisor page all season, computed from their log, so the number that decides a future spend is watched by the client continuously rather than presented by us at the end. Business outcome measurement is the paper tally, nine weeks in 2026 and the same calendar weeks in 2027. If they will not run the tally, the outcome is unmeasurable and the study says so rather than promising a measured result.

failure_modes.mode: The canon disagrees with the live website after a price or schedule change
failure_modes.detection: canon-drift, weekly, plus the February re-certification before the season opens on March 7th
failure_modes.behaviour: The affected red list branch flips to ABSTAIN automatically until a human adjudicates. The tool degrades to 'ask a person', never to a stale answer.
failure_modes.why_this_matters: A wrong number carrying a genuine citation reads as MORE verified than a wrong number with none.

failure_modes.mode: The vessel serving a departure is unknown or the map row has expired
failure_modes.detection: UNKNOWN is a stored value and effective_to is checked on every lookup
failure_modes.behaviour: The accessibility branch abstains and routes to a named human. This is a correct answer, not a failure, and the agent sees the reason.
failure_modes.why_this_matters: Accessibility is the one branch with no catcher upstream of the dock, and it has a dignity cost rather than only a dollar one.

failure_modes.mode: Two seasons are live and the agent asks a price question with no date
failure_modes.detection: The engine refuses to infer a season
failure_modes.behaviour: With no date it abstains. With a date that lands in two live products it returns BOTH answers, each labelled with its season and its effective range. A certification case asserts this returns two answers rather than one.
failure_modes.why_this_matters: The 4 Hour Kenai Fjords Wildlife Cruise is 149 dollars for 2026 and the 4 Hour Spring Wildlife Cruise is 109 dollars for March 20th to May 16th 2027, so the question has two correct answers today.

failure_modes.mode: The network is down at the desk, or Neon is down
failure_modes.detection: Service worker and a failed POST
failure_modes.behaviour: Answers keep working, because canon.json is inlined and the app is a cached PWA. Misses queue in IndexedDB and sync on reconnect. Nothing on the answer path depends on a server being up.
failure_modes.why_this_matters: A lookup that stops working on a bad connection at the harbour is a lookup nobody trusts twice.

failure_modes.mode: Cloudflare Access is down and nobody can log in
failure_modes.behaviour: The already installed PWA keeps serving from cache for the session, and the printed fallback card carries the four branches at their common inputs with the same canon version stamp.
failure_modes.why_this_matters: The desk runs 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. seven days a week year round (c2), so there is no window where being down is free.

failure_modes.mode: The agent enters the booking contents wrongly, since there is no booking integration
failure_modes.detection: The answer card echoes the inputs back above the sentence
failure_modes.behaviour: The wrong input is visible before the sentence is spoken. Each input field carries the published sentence that makes it matter.
failure_modes.why_this_matters: This is the honest residual risk of refusing to scope an integration against a vendor nobody has verified, and it belongs in the open, not in a footnote.

failure_modes.mode: Somebody later wants a model wired in behind the four red list branches
failure_modes.detection: test_redlist_never_reaches_retriever fails, and it is a required check
failure_modes.behaviour: The build does not merge. The filter is code with a contract test, not a prompt instruction and not a policy document.
failure_modes.why_this_matters: A safety property that exists only in a prompt is a safety property that gets edited out on a Friday.

failure_modes.mode: Nobody at Major Marine runs the paper tally sheet
failure_modes.detection: Week two, from an empty clipboard
failure_modes.behaviour: We say so in writing at that point. The outcome becomes unmeasurable and the study never promises a measured result on an unrun baseline.
failure_modes.why_this_matters: An unmeasurable claim is a different kind of claim, not a smaller one.

failure_modes.mode: The miss log lands below the retrieval gate
failure_modes.detection: The gate counters on the supervisor page, all season
failure_modes.behaviour: We say so in writing, we do not invoice, and the published conclusion is that this business needed a rule set and not an AI.
failure_modes.why_this_matters: A gate that can only pass is decoration on a decision already taken.

build_vs_buy.why: Cloudflare Access. Free at this seat count, group based, and it matches a workforce that is rebuilt inside a three month hiring window every year. Writing our own user store would be the single most pointless line in this budget.
Cloudflare Pages. The answer path is a static bundle, so the commodity is the whole delivery mechanism.
Cloudflare Workers. One vendor for hosting, identity and the API keeps the operating surface at one login for a company with no IT department.
Neon Postgres. The miss log is a few thousand rows a season. Managed Postgres with a US region pin and a scheduled delete job is the boring correct answer.

build_vs_buy.component: Version control, CI and the handover vehicle
build_vs_buy.why: GitHub and Actions. It also gives the canon a dated, diffable, reviewable history for free, which is exactly what 'one canonical dated source' needs, and the repo transfers to them at the end.
Their existing spreadsheet. The policy owner already knows how to use it, and a bespoke admin UI would be a week of build to replace a tool they open every day.
httpx and selectolax, open source. Thirty plain HTML pages needs a library, not a product, and it is plumbing rather than an AI website checker.

build_vs_buy.component: The decision table engine and its cell schema
build_vs_buy.why: THE DIFFERENTIATOR. It encodes Major Marine's own published policy across four branches with a finite input space, and nobody sells that. It is also the only component in the proposal whose acceptance bar can be certified at 100 percent on an exhaustive enumeration rather than sampled, which is the entire reason this build survives.

build_vs_buy.component: The red list router and its contract test
build_vs_buy.why: The safety property is bespoke to these four branches, and it has to be a required CI check on our own code to be worth anything. No product enforces 'never let a retriever near a refund clock at this company'.

build_vs_buy.component: The canon schema with mandatory verbatim sentence, URL and season
build_vs_buy.why: Season scoping of every dated and priced fact is a hard requirement here because two seasons are live at once, and no off the shelf knowledge base makes season a required field or fails a build without it. A knowledge base returns a page. This has to return a decided answer over four inputs, with the sentence.

The acceptance bar IS the product. A generic test runner does not know what the cross product of their four branches is, and the enumerated, signed off cell table is the artefact the client is really buying.

It does not exist anywhere to buy or to copy. Nothing public provides it and the evidence says the internal copies disagree. It is the highest value asset in the engagement and they keep it whatever happens next.

build_vs_buy.component: The miss log schema and the client side redactor
build_vs_buy.why: The PII rule is specific to their data, guest names, booking references, mobility and dietary facts. A generic form product would happily store all four in one row, which is the thing we are designing against.

Small, and its whole job is a constraint. The verbatim sentence is the largest element and there is no free text field anywhere in the render path, which is a design decision no component library ships with.

build_vs_buy.component: Any model, vector store or embedding pipeline
build_vs_buy.why: Neither built nor bought in phase one, because none is used. Stated here so the line is unambiguous. If the option is ever exercised, the base model and the index are commodities to rent, never to build.

build_vs_buy.component: A guest facing tourism chatbot of the kind vendors sell into this category
build_vs_buy.why: If it is ever earned it should be bought rather than built, and it is not in this scope. It sits first in the Later lane gated on a full season of internal evidence. The honest reason it is not first is that it puts confident wrong answers on the guest side of a thirty year locally owned reputation before any eval set exists.

goals: A first week hire in the March 2027 cohort answers a refund clock, an accessibility question, a shuttle eligibility question and a dietary window correctly in their first hour on the desk, without waiting on a veteran.

100 percent agreement with published policy across an EXHAUSTIVE enumeration of the four branches, certified before ship and re-certified every February before the season opens on March 7th. Not a threshold on a sample.
No answer is ever returned without the verbatim published sentence and its source URL, asserted in the library on every response rather than requested in a prompt.
Every dated or priced fact carries a season, and a question with two correct answers in two live seasons returns both rather than choosing one.
Abstain rather than guess. Every unknown input combination and every unknown vessel returns 'no published rule for this case, escalate to <named role>' and writes a miss log row.

Three assets Major Marine keeps regardless of what is ever built next. One canonical dated policy source, one authoritative vessel to departure map, and a written record of what their own desk actually gets asked.
A baseline that exists. The paper tally starts this week, in the final nine weeks of the 2026 season, so the 2027 measurement has something to compare against.
The retrieval gate is computed from their own log, shown on a page they watch all season, and it can fail. If it fails we say so in writing and do not invoice.

non_goals.item: Any integration with the booking engine
non_goals.reason: The vendor is unidentified and is never named or guessed, so the integration surface is unscopeable from public facts and any effort number would be invented. Phase one is a standalone tool with manual entry of booking contents, said plainly.

non_goals.item: Any model, vector store, embedding or generated prose in phase one
non_goals.reason: The four funded branches have the highest cost of error in the business, a finite input space, and answers already published by the company itself. Determinism wins outright and there is nothing for a model to add except fluency.

non_goals.item: Snippet retrieval as a funded phase
non_goals.reason: It is an OPTION with a number on its gate, not a phase. Its eval set does not exist and it can only exist after a season of real questions is logged and labelled, which makes it a 2028 tool at the earliest.

non_goals.item: Any guest facing surface, chat widget, web bot or public search box
non_goals.reason: Staff facing only. A wrong answer in front of a guest has no human filter, and the human reading the returned sentence is the entire safety argument.

non_goals.item: Anything on the phone line, voice agent, IVR or call recording
non_goals.reason: The line is a revenue channel, packages are bookable by phone only (c1), all discounts must be booked direct (c3), and a verified reservation page routes bookings inside twelve hours to a call (c29). Recording also adds consent law and buys phase one nothing.

non_goals.item: Self-serve cancellation or online change
non_goals.reason: It needs the booking vendor we refuse to guess at, and no operator in this market offers it, so it is a field-wide gap and not a Major Marine defect.

non_goals.item: A self-serve package configurator
non_goals.reason: No published volume denominator, an unscopeable integration, and phone-only sitting next to a direct-only discount rule and a named Director of Sales is at least as consistent with a deliberate margin decision as with a defect. Removing a revenue mechanism while calling it a fix is not something to do on a guess.

non_goals.item: A seat allocation optimiser
non_goals.reason: It is constraint solving rather than AI, and there is zero evidence the current staff assigned process (c18) causes anyone pain. Building on speculation ends with nothing to measure.

non_goals.item: A disruption console as a product, and any generated disruption notice
non_goals.reason: Its entitlement math is this same decision table applied to a list, and its event frequency is unpublished. Cruises go out rain or shine and are only cancelled for unsafe sea conditions (c11). Count the events on the tally sheet first. For the notice itself the stated goal is consistency, and a template with merge fields is consistent by construction while a model is consistent only under supervision.

non_goals.item: Editing their live website
non_goals.reason: The parking contradiction and the stale 2021 copy get adjudicated INTO the canon, which is a content operations output. Pushing corrections back onto the live site needs their CMS, which is not scoped, and it is a separate conversation. These defects are evidence for corpus readiness, never a headline.

non_goals.item: Rollout to the veteran shoreside team
non_goals.reason: The measured effect this design rests on is concentrated in novices and near zero in experienced staff. A Vice President at 22 years and a Maintenance Director at 15 do not need it, and measuring adoption on them would dilute a working tool into an average that looks like failure.

non_goals.item: An hours saved dashboard or an hours saved business case
non_goals.reason: The reservations desk headcount is unpublished, so any hours figure before the tally sheet runs is an invented denominator.

non_goals.item: A review response tool
non_goals.reason: A 61,459 call audit across 12 models measured responding to reviews at +0.1 percentage points on how models recommend, statistically equivalent to zero. In that channel the tooling buys nothing, and we hand the finding over with no invoice attached.

design.riskiest_assumption: THAT THE VESSEL TO DEPARTURE MAP IS STABLE ENOUGH TO ENCODE AT ALL. The whole accessibility branch assumes there is one internal source that says which boat runs which departure, and that the answer is known far enough ahead to be worth telling a guest. Two things say it may not be. Nothing public provides the map, and the FAQ names a vessel running the 12:30 pm 4 Hour departure that the eight vessel fleet page does not list, which is direct evidence that internally the answer lives in more than one place and the copies disagree. Whether that vessel is chartered, retired or simply omitted is UNRESOLVED. Vessel assignment also plausibly moves with maintenance and charters. If it moves day to day, the accessibility branch abstains permanently, and that is the branch with the highest cost of error in the business and the only one with no catcher upstream of the dock. Losing it does not shrink the build, it removes the strongest single reason to buy it. Everything else on the risk list threatens the measurement. This one threatens the design.
design.spike_to_retire_it: FIVE WORKING DAYS, unbilled, before any contract is signed and before a line of the accessibility branch is written. Zero build. Day one, a 90 minute session with the named operations owner asking one question, where does vessel assignment live today, and photographing it in whatever form it turns out to be, a whiteboard, a spreadsheet, a printed sheet or somebody's memory. Days two and three, reconstruct the last 14 operating days of the 2026 season from that source. For each of the seven departure slots on each day, name the vessel, and count how many of those cells the source can fill with certainty. Day four, run the same exercise forward across the first 14 operating days of the 2027 season from March 7th, and count how many can be committed now. Day five, the written result and the decision. THE PASS BAR IS PRE-COMMITTED IN WRITING BEFORE DAY ONE. At least 80 percent of the historical cells resolvable from one source, the vessel identity known at least 24 hours ahead for at least 90 percent of the forward departures, and the 12:30 pm departure discrepancy resolved to a stated answer by a named person. IF IT FAILS, the accessibility branch ships as ABSTAIN ALWAYS with a routing script to a named human, the funded scope drops to three branches, and the ask drops with it. We say that before invoicing rather than after. Two cheap things ride in the same window at no extra cost. The canon-drift crawl runs once across the roughly thirty pages and COUNTS the conflicts, because four were found in one afternoon by an outsider and the content operations estimate depends on whether the real number is nearer eight or nearer sixty. And the four branch boundaries get agreed with the client on paper, which fixes the cell count and, just as importantly, fixes the scope of what counts as a miss before we are the ones who benefit from a fatter miss log.
