estimates.does_it_fit_the_18000_ask: YES, on one condition stated up front. At 18 to 26 of our person-days, 18,000 dollars fixed is roughly 690 to 1,000 dollars a day, which is a real rate for a scope this tightly bounded. It fits BECAUSE the content operations half is largely THEIR owner's time and not ours. Only they know which parking price is the right one, so adjudication is theirs by nature and we build the tooling and run the process. If Major Marine will not commit the 20 to 34 named owner hours, the scope does not fit the ask, and we would say that rather than absorb it, because absorbing it is how a fixed price turns into a bad delivery. Two other things would break the fit and both are checked at the spike. A conflict count far above the four already found, and a vessel map that needs building from scratch rather than reconciling.
what_narrows_the_range: The spike result on the vessel map. It is the difference between four branches and three, and it moves the effort estimate more than anything else on this list.
The counted conflict list from one canon-drift crawl. Four conflicts were found in one afternoon by an outsider. Eight and sixty are very different content operations jobs.
The agreed branch boundaries, which fix the cell count. It is estimated at 300 to 900 cells and it becomes a known number in a day once the four branches are drawn on paper.
A named policy owner and a named operations owner, with committed hours on a calendar rather than a promise. This is the single largest driver of elapsed time.
Whether they run an identity provider or need the one time PIN fallback, which is a day either way and worth knowing early.
Nine weeks of tally data, which turns the escalation rate and the misquote count from an assumption into a measurement.

delivery_shape.walking_skeleton: ONE branch, shuttle eligibility, end to end and actually running, with everything else on crutches. The agent logs in through Cloudflare Access, opens Desk Answer, picks Shuttle, enters the departure date, the product and time, the hours of notice and whether an advance reservation exists, and gets back either the verbatim published sentence with its URL, its season and the canon version, or an abstain naming the human to escalate to. The abstain writes a redacted row through the Worker into Neon. canon-build compiles the shuttle rules from the workbook, canon-certify enumerates the full shuttle cross product in GitHub Actions and blocks the deploy on a single disagreement, and the red list router ships in the FIRST commit with its contract test and a NullRetriever that throws if anything ever calls it. Why shuttle first, the input space is the smallest of the four, every fact in it is already verified, it has the sharpest guest cost of the set because a missed sailing is a no-show and a no-show is completely non-refundable, and it exercises abstain, verbatim, season scoping and the miss log in one slice. DELIBERATELY STUBBED at this stage, the other three branches, the vessel map which returns UNKNOWN for every lookup so accessibility abstains 100 percent of the time and the abstain path is proven before it matters, the supervisor page, the drift crawler, and the redactor which is a first pass only.
delivery_shape.then_flesh_out: Dietary next, because it is the smallest remaining table and it proves the two-season rule cleanly, the 4 Hour has no meal while the three long cruises take a vegetarian request at the time of reservation. Then refunds and change fees, which is the largest cell count and the most cash exposure and where the two sentence change fee rule and the no-show rule must stay structurally separate so the table can never splice them into one answer. Accessibility LAST, deliberately, because it is gated on the spike outcome and on the vessel map delivery date, and it is the one branch we are willing to ship as a permanent abstain if the map is not there.
delivery_shape.then_mvp: Certified phase one in the desk's hands before March 7th 2027. All four branches, or three plus a declared and visible accessibility abstain. canon-certify green across the exhaustive cross product with the cell table signed by a named internal policy owner. canon-drift on a weekly cron with the auto-abstain teeth wired. The supervisor page live with the four gate counters and the sampling day scheduler. Client side redaction plus the server side second pass, the 400 day retention job running, and the PII rule signed before the first real entry. The PWA installed on the desk machines and tested with the network pulled. The printed fallback card laminated and stamped with the canon version. A 40 minute training session with the March cohort, recorded, so the next cohort gets it without us. Then the handover, the repository transferred to a Major Marine account, the canon and the vessel map theirs, the miss log exported to CSV on one command and portable to any vendor including one that is not us.
delivery_shape.what_ships_that_is_not_software: The tally sheet, the reconciled canon, the vessel map and the printed card. Three of those four have standalone value on a day when no software has been installed anywhere, which is the honest way to describe a large part of what the 18,000 buys.

architecture.caption: The funded path has no model in it. A question from the desk hits the red list router first, so refunds and change fees, accessibility, shuttle eligibility and dietary windows go straight to the decision table and never reach a retriever, enforced by a contract test rather than by a prompt. The table reads the policy canon, which is built from Major Marine's own published pages, carries a date and a season on every priced fact, and returns the verbatim sentence with its URL for the agent to read out loud. It writes only to the miss log. Where an input combination has no published rule, or where the vessel serving a departure is not known, the table abstains and routes to a named person, which is the correct answer rather than a failure. The one AI node on this diagram is the option, and it is not funded, not built, and only ever discussed if the miss log clears a number agreed in writing beforehand.

now.item: A paper tally sheet on the reservations desk for the final nine weeks of the 2026 season. Question asked, time to answer, escalated or not, to whom, and the verbatim wording where the agent has time to write it. Zero software, zero cost, starts this week.
now.metric: A sheet returned for 100 percent of staffed days from the start date to October 11th, plus two supervisor-logged full days a month where every question is written down rather than only the ones a busy agent remembered. Outputs are the three numbers that do not exist anywhere today, median time to answer a policy or eligibility question, escalation rate for a first-season agent, and count of policy misquotes that reached a guest. It also produces the first count of re-routes into Resurrection Bay and late-train transfers, and the first miss log entries.
now.why_first: It is free and the window shuts. Products fall away on a ladder, the 8.5 Hour ended September 7th, the 7.5 Hour ends September 13th, the 6 Hour September 21st, and only the 4 Hour runs to October 11th, so every week of delay costs a week of the only observation window that exists before March. There is no baseline today, so without this the outcome can be modelled and never measured. It also carries its own off-ramp, if the sheets come back showing the desk barely escalates and misquotes are not happening, that finding saves the whole project and we would rather find it in September than in March. Honest caveat stated up front, these nine weeks are shoulder season with three departure slots already ended on August 23rd, so this count is a floor and never a peak.

now.item: Corpus reconciliation. One canonical, dated, owned policy source, built from a crawl that finds every conflicting statement, with a named internal owner adjudicating each one. Includes season scoping of every dated and priced fact, because two seasons are live at once, and a review cadence with a real trigger before each season opens and after any price or schedule change.
now.metric: Every conflict the crawl finds is adjudicated, dated and signed by a named owner, with zero unresolved contradictions remaining on the four branches the table answers. Known starting set includes the two pages giving different parking prices, a live 2026 booking page still carrying copy about a cruise being new in 2021 and unavailable in 2020, a product with a live 2026 page that is missing from the five-product index, and the 4 Hour priced at 149 dollars for 2026 alongside the 4 Hour Spring Wildlife Cruise already published at 109 dollars for March 20th to May 16th, 2027.
now.why_first: This is the largest item of hidden scope in the whole proposal and it was not costed anywhere before now. It is content operations rather than modelling, and only someone inside the company knows which parking price is the right one. It has to land before anything else reads from it, and it is a win on its own terms, since one canonical dated source improves the website, the two hotel front desks and the dock on a day when no software has been installed anywhere.

now.item: The authoritative vessel-to-departure map, with a named internal owner and a date, plus a written ruling on whether vessel assignment is stable across maintenance and charters. If it is not stable, the honest design is that the tool never answers accessibility and routes it to a named person.
now.metric: Either a signed, dated map covering every scheduled departure, or a written decision that assignment is not stable enough to publish, in which case the accessibility branch ships as abstain-to-a-named-human. Both outcomes are a pass. What is not a pass is an unowned map. Includes a ruling on the unresolved case where the FAQ describes Rachel Marie running the 12:30 pm 4 Hour departure while the eight-vessel fleet page does not list it, which we state as unresolved and never as a claim about what the vessel is or is not.
now.why_first: It is the longest client-side lead time in the engagement and the only dependency that may turn out not to exist at all, so it starts on day one and runs in parallel with our build. Every accessibility, seating and capacity answer joins to it. Accessibility carries the highest cost of error in the business and it is the only branch with no intermediate catcher, since a guest who is told a departure is accessible when the vessel running it is not discovers it at the gangway, where nothing recovers it. Five vessels are published as accessible on the first deck inside the main cabin only, the outside decks are not, and no vessel takes a motorized wheelchair, so the answer is worthless without knowing which hull is on which sailing.

now.item: WALKING SKELETON. One branch, refund clocks and change fees, running end to end on a real desk question. The agent enters what the booking contains, the tool returns the clock, the fee and the verbatim published sentence with its source URL for the agent to read out loud. Anything outside the table returns no published rule for this case, escalate to the named role, and writes a miss log entry.
now.metric: 100 percent agreement with published policy across an exhaustive enumeration of that branch's input cross product, not a sample, covering the 72 hour cruise-only clock, the 7 day cruise and hotel clock, the 21 day clock once motorcoach or train is added, the 3 percent card fee retained on cancellation, one free date change to 24 hours out then 15 dollars per person, and the no-show rule. Second hard metric, zero responses returned without a verbatim published sentence and its URL attached, checked as an assertion on every single response.
now.why_first: It is the thinnest slice that touches every component and actually runs, the canonical source, the table, the verbatim-source assertion, the default-deny abstain route and the miss log. It was chosen over the other three branches for one specific reason, it needs no vessel map, so the single dependency that may not exist can't block first light. It also carries the clearest hard-dollar benefit in the build. Quoting the 72 hour cruise-only clock to a guest holding a 21 day transportation package means refunding money the company did not owe on a booking whose third-party transportation it may already be committed to, and that is the one error direction that costs the company cash rather than the guest.

now.item: The remaining three branches, completing the four-branch decision table. Accessibility by vessel, shuttle eligibility, and dietary windows by product. No model anywhere in it.
now.metric: 100 percent agreement across an exhaustive enumeration of the full input cross product, signed off cell by cell by a named internal policy owner before the tool ships, kept as a regression suite that is re-run on every content change. Default deny on everything else. The accessibility branch additionally abstains whenever the vessel serving a departure is not known with certainty. Worked examples the table has to get right every time, the shuttle is excluded from the 8:00 a.m. 6 Hour cruise, needs advance reservation and 24 hours notice, the terminal loop only runs 7:00 to 9:45 a.m. so it is a partial fallback for a cruise ship guest and none at all for a guest who parked, and the walk is 0.6 miles from Harbor 360 and 0.8 from the South Harbor office with luggage before an 8:00 a.m. boarding. Vegetarian requests are at the time of reservation on the 6, 7.5 and 8.5 Hour cruises and the 4 Hour has no meal at all.
now.why_first: These three plus refunds are the four highest-cost-of-error questions in the business, they are finite, and their answers are already published by the company itself. This is the only component in the entire proposal whose acceptance bar can be certified rather than sampled, which is why it is funded and why no model touches it. A wrong shuttle answer converts into a missed sailing, and a missed sailing is a no-show, which the published policy makes completely non-refundable, so the cost there is a guest's whole day and the company's reputation.

now.item: The miss log as a real governance object rather than a backlog. Verbatim capture of the question as asked, a labelled correct answer from a named internal authority with its source page, a held-out split never looked at during development, deliberate out-of-corpus cases the system should refuse, the supervisor sampling arm that corrects its own selection bias, re-labelling each season, and a PII rule agreed before the first entry is written.
now.metric: PII rule and read-access decision agreed and written down before entry one, since the log will capture names, booking references, mobility information and dietary information, and the last two are health adjacent. Labelling kept current rather than accruing as an unlabelled pile, measured as labelled share of entries. Supervisor sample days actually run, two per month. Volume written down in advance at roughly 150 to 300 labelled items across a full season.
now.why_first: This is the single most valuable thing in the whole engagement and it is one paragraph of specification away from being theatre. Without labelled answers, a held-out split and deliberate refusable cases, there is no eval set, and with no eval set nothing above the rules rung is ever fundable on evidence. It is also their data in their format, portable, and they can take it to any vendor including one that is not us, or to nobody.

now.item: A stop-doing finding handed over free, with no invoice attached. In the channel where AI assistants recommend operators, tooling bought to respond to reviews buys nothing measurable.
now.metric: Dollars not spent on review-response tooling sold on the promise of moving AI recommendation. A 61,459-call audit across 12 models measured responding to reviews at plus 0.1 percentage points on recommendation probability, statistically equivalent to zero, against about plus 32 points for guest rating and minus 30 for price. Stated precisely, that audit measures how models recommend, so it does not prove review responses are worthless to human readers.
now.why_first: It costs nothing, it ships with the study, and it is worth more to them than several things on this page that carry a price. It also sets the tone for every gate below, we would rather tell them what not to buy than sell them the next thing.

next.item: Certification and re-certification before the 2027 cohort touches it. The full regression suite re-run against the reconciled source, every cell re-signed, season scoping re-checked with two seasons live at once, and the abstain route tested rather than assumed.
next.metric: Regression suite green at 100 percent, and every dated or priced cell unambiguous about which season it belongs to, both completed before the first published 2027 sailing. Zero cells where the 2026 price and the 2027 price could both be returned for the same question.

next.item: Rollout aimed at the March cohort only. First-season Customer Service and Sales Staff, deliberately not the veterans.
next.metric: The three tally numbers re-measured in the same calendar weeks as the 2026 baseline, weeks one through six after the cohort starts, looking for a fall in median time to answer, a fall in escalation rate for first-season agents, and a fall in misquotes reaching a guest, with no fall in guest experience. Adoption measured as share of first-season desk hires using it in weeks one to six. The rollout deliberately does not target staff at 22, 15, 11 and 8 years, because the mechanism this build rests on concentrates in novices and is near zero in experienced workers, so a rollout to everyone would dilute into an average that looks like failure while the tool worked exactly as measured.

next.item: A full season of miss log accrual and labelling across the 2027 season, roughly March to October, with the supervisor sampling arm running throughout.
next.metric: The three numbers that decide the retrieval gate, share of logged desk questions falling outside the table, count of distinct question types recurring three or more times, and count of labelled items after de-duplication. The 2026 nine-week tally is a shoulder-season floor and is explicitly not used to read this gate.

next.item: Counted disruption frequency across a full season, as a measurement and not a build.
next.metric: A real count of re-routes limited to Resurrection Bay that triggered a partial refund at the Captain's discretion, and of late-train transfers, over one full season. Cruises go out rain or shine and are only cancelled for unsafe sea conditions, so this number may well come back small, and small is a finding that keeps the batch mode unbuilt.

next.item: Read the retrieval option gate at the close of the 2027 season and publish the result either way, invoiced or not invoiced.
next.metric: A written result against the three pre-agreed numbers. If it clears, retrieval is scoped for the March 2028 cohort. If it does not clear, the published conclusion is that this business needed a rule set and not an AI, and nothing is invoiced.

later.item: A guest-facing chatbot on the website and messaging channels, gated on a full season of internal evidence. If it is ever built it runs on a whitelist with abstain-to-human as the default and never answers a refund, accessibility, shuttle or dietary question.
later.metric: Before any guest sees it, abstention recall on a deliberately constructed out-of-corpus set, and zero outputs of any kind on the four high-cost branches, enforced by a topic filter in code rather than by an instruction. The value metric is guest questions answered outside the published 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. window, which nothing else on this roadmap touches. The named comparable is a day-cruise operator reporting 10 staff hours saved a month and 60 percent of questions answered, and the same vendor's homepage claims 95 percent where its own customer measured 60, so the comparable is read at its measured number and never at its marketing one.

later.item: Disruption batch mode, folded into the table rather than built as a standalone console. The entitlement math is the same decision table applied to a list, showing who is affected, which remaining departures have room and what each booking is owed, with a template carrying merge fields for the notification. Gated on a counted event frequency. Covers the late-train transfer case as well as a Captain's re-route.
later.metric: Counted events per season from the 2027 measurement, against a threshold agreed in advance. The notification is a template and never a model, because the stated goal is consistency and a template is consistent by construction while a model is consistent only under supervision. Value metric is time from the Captain's decision to every affected guest notified, and consistency of what each guest was told.

later.item: A self-serve package configurator taking packages off the phone. Gated first on a conversation, not on a build.
later.metric: The gate is a question for the Director of Sales, whether packages being bookable by phone only, alongside a rule that all discounts must be booked direct and are not valid through third parties, is a deliberate margin and upsell decision rather than a defect. If it is deliberate, this item dies here and that is the right outcome. If it is not, it still needs the booking vendor identified before any effort number is honest, and a published package volume before any revenue ceiling is anything but a guess. Value metric would be packages assembled and paid for outside the 8 to 6 window with the direct-only discount rule preserved.

later.item: Seat allocation support, gated on any evidence at all that the current process hurts.
later.metric: A counted number from the tally or the miss log, staff time spent on seating or special requests that could not be honoured. Seats are assigned by staff before the cruise and special requests are not guaranteed, and there is no evidence at all today that this causes anyone pain. If the count comes back at zero, this stays unbuilt, which is the point of it being on this lane rather than in the build.

later.item: Staff-facing snippet retrieval over the reconciled corpus for the March 2028 cohort, verbatim source mandatory, no composed prose, staff facing only. Priced now as an option, built only if the gate clears.
later.metric: Three acceptance numbers pre-committed in writing before any build, grounded correctness on the held-out labelled set at 90 percent or better, abstention recall on a deliberately constructed out-of-corpus set at 95 percent or better, and zero tolerance on a red list, no output of any kind on refund amounts and clocks, accessibility by vessel, shuttle eligibility or dietary windows, enforced by a topic filter in code before the retriever is ever called. A kill switch reverting to the decision table alone, tested before launch rather than assumed.

later.item: One canonical source serving three counters, the reservations desk, the dock, and the two hotel front desks that already answer some version of the same cruise questions.
later.metric: Same answer at every counter, measured by spot checks against the canonical source. Near zero build cost once reconciliation is done, since the asset already exists at that point and only the reach changes.

roadmap.gates: Five gates, each earned by measured results from the one before it, and every one of them capable of stopping the money. GATE 0, THE TALLY GATE, before any build spend. If nobody at the company will run the paper sheet for nine weeks, the honest position is that the outcome can't be measured, and the study says so rather than promising a measured result. An unmeasurable claim is not a smaller claim, it is a different kind of claim. If the sheets do come back and show a desk that barely escalates and rarely misquotes, that is grounds for them to stop before a line of code is written, and we would say so. GATE 1, CERTIFICATION, before the tool goes anywhere near a live desk. 100 percent agreement with published policy across an exhaustive enumeration of the input cross product rather than a threshold on a sample, every cell signed by a named internal policy owner, an assertion on every response that no answer returns without its verbatim published sentence and URL, default deny writing a miss log entry on anything outside the table, and the vessel map either signed or the accessibility branch shipping as abstain. GATE 2, SEASON READINESS, before the March cohort touches it. Regression suite green after re-running against the reconciled source, season scoping verified with two seasons live at once, abstain route and escalation path tested rather than assumed. GATE 3, THE RETRIEVAL OPTION GATE, read at the close of the 2027 season, numeric and capable of failing. All three of the following, at least 15 percent of logged desk questions falling outside the table, AND at least 20 distinct question types recurring three or more times, AND at least 150 labelled items after de-duplication. The client sets the final figures. What is not negotiable is that a number exists and that it can fail. THE SYMMETRIC OUTCOME IS WRITTEN INTO THE SAME DOCUMENT. If the log lands below any one of the three, we say so in writing, we do not invoice, nothing is built, and the published conclusion is that this business needed a rule set and not an AI. Three things neutralise the obvious conflict of interest, that the party who benefits from clearing the gate is the party who designs the table that decides what counts as a miss. The table's boundaries are agreed with them up front so the scope of a miss is not ours to set after the fact. The log is their data in their format, portable to any vendor including one that is not us. Phase one also has to be worth buying standalone with no obligation, which at 18,000 dollars fixed it is, since they keep three assets either way, one canonical dated policy source, one authoritative vessel map, and a written record of what their own desk actually gets asked. GATE 4, THE LATER LANE GATES, each named on its own item. The chatbot needs a full season of internal evidence and a measured abstention rate before a guest ever sees it. The batch mode needs a counted event frequency. The configurator needs a conversation about whether phone-only is deliberate, and a deliberate answer kills it. Seat allocation needs any evidence at all that it currently hurts. Nothing on the kill list comes back through any of these gates.
need_from_you: SOMEONE TO RUN THE TALLY. One named person on the desk who fills the paper sheet on every staffed day from this week to October 11th, plus a supervisor who logs every question on two randomly chosen full days a month. That second part is not bureaucracy, it corrects the log's own selection bias, since under-logging is guaranteed at peak and peak is exactly when the errors happen. This is the dependency that decides whether anything downstream is measurable, and it is on your side of the line, not ours.

A NAMED OWNER TO ADJUDICATE CONFLICTING PUBLISHED FACTS. Someone with the authority to rule which parking price is right, to retire the 2020 and 2021 copy still sitting on a live 2026 booking page, to decide whether the product with a live page belongs on the five-product index, and to keep the 2026 and 2027 prices from colliding while both seasons are selling. Only somebody inside the company knows which one is correct, and this owner also signs off every cell of the decision table before it ships.

A NAMED OWNER FOR THE VESSEL-TO-DEPARTURE MAP, WITH A DATE. This data does not exist in verified published form and, on the evidence, may not exist internally in one place either. It needs a ruling on whether assignment is stable across maintenance and charters, and a ruling on the case where the FAQ describes a vessel running the 12:30 pm 4 Hour departure that the fleet page does not list. If it turns out not to be stable, say so and the tool never answers accessibility, it routes to a named person. That is a good outcome, not a failure.

LABELLING HOURS FROM A NAMED INTERNAL AUTHORITY. Every miss log entry needs a correct answer with its source page, produced by someone at the company rather than by us and never by a model. This is real hours from people who are busy, it belongs in the plan with a name against it, and if it is refused then the miss log is a backlog, retrieval is unscoped, and the honest response is to say so and not build it.

A PII RULE AGREED BEFORE THE FIRST ENTRY. The log captures questions verbatim, which means names, booking references, mobility information and dietary information. Field-level discipline or redaction at capture, a retention rule, and a decision about who may read it, all settled before entry one rather than after.

AGREEMENT ON THE TABLE'S BOUNDARIES UP FRONT. What counts as inside the table and what counts as a miss is agreed with you before phase one starts, so the number the retrieval gate is read against is not one we can move afterwards.
ONE DECISION-MAKER FOR THE GATES. Every gate above is your off-ramp, and off-ramps only work when one named person can call them.
roadmap.sequencing_rationale: Sequenced on cost of delay divided by size, with one correction that RICE and WSJF both handle badly. COST OF DELAY HERE IS A STEP FUNCTION, NOT A SLOPE. Peak seasonal hiring runs January 15th to April 15th and about 60 seasonal staff arrive inside that window every year, so the desk this build serves is rebuilt from novices every spring. Either the tool is in the 2027 cohort's hands before their season opens or it is worth nothing at all until 2028. There is no partial credit for landing in May. So the ordering question is not what is most valuable, it is what fits before the cliff. FIRST, THE FREE THING WITH THE CLOSING WINDOW. The paper tally is size zero and its window shuts on October 11th when the last product stops running. It creates the baseline that does not exist, counts the disruption events that decide whether a batch mode is ever worth building, and starts the miss log before any tool exists. Nothing else on the roadmap is free, and nothing else expires in nine weeks. SECOND, THE THING EVERYTHING READS FROM. Corpus reconciliation is the largest piece of uncosted scope in the original proposal and every other item depends on it. It is also the item with standalone value on a day when no software has been installed anywhere. THIRD, THE LONGEST CLIENT-SIDE LEAD TIME, STARTED IN PARALLEL. The vessel map is the one dependency that may not exist at all, and what eats a calendar is almost never the engineering, it is waiting on a decision only the client can make. It starts on day one and it is allowed to end in an abstain. FOURTH, THE WALKING SKELETON, AND IT WAS CHOSEN TO DODGE THE RISKY DEPENDENCY. Refunds and change fees run end to end first because that branch needs no vessel map, so first light can't be blocked by the one input that might turn out to be unstable, and because it carries the clearest hard-dollar benefit, the refund issued in the generous direction on money the company did not owe. Accessibility carries the higher cost of error and comes second precisely because it depends on the map. THE TWO-SEASON CORRECTION IS THE OTHER SEQUENCING DECISION AND IT COST THE ORIGINAL PLAN A WHOLE YEAR. The retrieval option can't reach the March 2027 cohort, because the questions that would justify it only accrue while a season runs. Collection runs roughly March to October 2027, labelling and build over that winter, and retrieval reaches the desk for the March 2028 cohort. Presenting both against one March 2027 clock would compress a two-season programme into one and would make this company look more ready than the evidence supports, which is the exact direction of drift this analysis had to correct twice. The nine-week 2026 tally is shoulder season with three departure slots already ended on August 23rd, so it is read as a floor and never used to settle the retrieval gate. LAST, WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT SEQUENCED. Everything on the Later lane carries a gate that can leave it unbuilt forever, and two of those gates are designed to kill their own item, the configurator dies if phone-only turns out to be a deliberate sales decision, and seat allocation stays unbuilt if the count comes back at zero.
roadmap.walking_skeleton: One branch, refund clocks and change fees, running end to end on a real question at the desk before the other three branches exist. The agent enters what the booking contains, cruise only, cruise and hotel, or transportation added, plus whether a date change has already been used and whether the guest sailed. The tool returns the clock, the fee and the verbatim published sentence with its source URL for the agent to read out loud. Anything outside the table returns no published rule for this case, escalate to the named role, and writes a miss log entry. It touches every component in the design, the canonical reconciled source, the decision table, the assertion that no answer leaves without its verbatim sentence and URL, the default-deny abstain route, and the miss log, so the whole shape is proven end to end while only one branch is encoded. It runs on crutches, the booking contents are typed in by hand, because the booking engine vendor is unidentified and no integration can honestly be scoped from what is public, and saying that keeps the estimate honest instead of hiding an integration nobody has scoped. Refunds were chosen over the other three branches for two reasons, it needs no vessel map so the one dependency that might not exist can't block first light, and it carries the clearest cash benefit, since quoting the 72 hour cruise-only clock to a guest holding a 21 day transportation package refunds money the company did not owe on a booking whose third-party transportation it may already be committed to.
not_on_any_lane: An AI voice agent on the reservations line. Killed on durable grounds rather than on latency. The line is a revenue channel where packages are sold and where bookings inside 12 hours are explicitly routed to a person, and the caller mix skews toward guests already in trouble. Nothing on this roadmap brings it back.

Free-text generation on refunds, accessibility, shuttle eligibility and dietary windows. Highest cost of error, finite input space, published answers, so determinism wins outright and the topic filter that enforces it lives in code rather than in an instruction.

Generation layered on retrieval inside the funded scope. It skips a rung, it roughly quadruples the modelled rate at which a wrong answer reaches a guest, and what it buys is fluency. Held as a separate third rung with its own gate, not folded into anything above.
A model drafting the disruption notification. The goal is consistency and a template with merge fields is consistent by construction.
A disruption console as a standalone product. Folded into the table as a batch mode on the Later lane, gated on a counted frequency.
A seat allocation optimiser as a funded build. It is constraint solving rather than AI, and there is no evidence today that the current process hurts anyone.
An AI website consistency checker sold as an AI build. It is a crawl, a diff and a link check, and it lives inside corpus reconciliation as plumbing on the Now lane.
high_integrity_dates: COMMITMENT. The reconciled source, the four-branch decision table and the miss log are certified and in the March cohort's hands before the first published 2027 sailing on March 20th, 2027. If the 2027 season opens earlier than that spring cruise, as the 2026 season did on March 7th, we hold to the earlier date. This is the one date on the roadmap that is a promise, and it is here because missing it costs the entire year, not a few weeks.

THEIR PUBLISHED CALENDAR, NOT OUR PROMISE. The 2026 season ends October 11th, which closes the tally window. The 8.5 Hour ended September 7th, the 7.5 Hour ends September 13th, the 6 Hour September 21st, and three departure slots ended August 23rd, so the observable operation shrinks every week between now and then.

THEIR PUBLISHED CALENDAR, NOT OUR PROMISE. Peak seasonal hiring runs January 15th to April 15th, which is the window that decides who is at the desk and the reason the delivery commitment above sits where it does.

NO OTHER DATES ARE COMMITTED. The retrieval option is not dated at all, because it is an option and not a phase. If its gate ever clears it is a March 2028 tool, and saying otherwise would compress two seasons into one.

roi.headline_verdict: AT THE 18,000 DOLLAR ASK THE CONSERVATIVE CASE DOES NOT CLEAR. It clears under most-likely and aggressive assumptions only. The recommended ask is therefore smaller, and it is priced as decision data that gates the bigger spend.
roi.cost_note: Five-year total cost of ownership, not sticker price, per Gartner TCO and the Forrester TEI four-part frame. Implementation is the 18,000 dollar fixed-price phase one ask exactly as sized in the economics pre-check, and it is not adjusted upward anywhere in this model. Training and change management is stated in HOURS and is entirely their people's time, about 84 hours in year one at the conservative population: 24 hours for an internal policy owner adjudicating the corpus contradictions and signing off one dated canonical source, 16 hours for operations to assemble and sign the vessel-to-departure map, about 11 hours to run the paper tally sheet for the final nine weeks of the 2026 season at roughly 10 minutes a shift, about 9 hours of cohort onboarding at 1.5 hours per first-season desk agent, and 24 hours of miss-log labelling by a named internal authority. Those hours are priced at assumed loaded rates and carried as a cost, never netted against the benefit. Ongoing run cost is real even though the funded build has no model in it and therefore has ZERO inference and ZERO token cost: it is the pre-season regression re-run and content refresh before March 7 each season, hosting and tooling, and the policy owner's review cadence, which the season-scoping problem makes annual and non-optional because two seasons are live at once on their own site today. Run cost accrues for 4.5 of the 5 years on a mid-year go-live convention. Contingency is 20 percent in the conservative case, 18 percent most-likely, 15 percent aggressive, at the top of the 15 to 20 band where the risk is organizational rather than technical, which is what it is here: the tally sheet, the corpus owner and the vessel map are all their work, not ours.

The strict-direction refund error, where a guest is refused a refund they were entitled to under the published policy. This is NOT a cash benefit, the company keeps that money. It is a reputation cost on a thirty-year locally owned family brand whose competitive position against a NYSE-listed operator in the same harbour is exactly that. It stays out of the formula.

The accessibility branch. roi.benefit_phasing: No day-one benefit anywhere in this model. The funded build lands in the March 2027 cohort's hands, so YEAR ONE IS ONE SEASON AND NOT TWELVE MONTHS OF STEADY STATE, and the season itself is March 7th to October 11th rather than a calendar year. Year one is discounted to 30 percent of run rate conservative, 45 percent most-likely, 60 percent aggressive, and that discount is ADOPTION, not calendar: a brand-new lookup in the hands of a cohort that is itself brand new, with the corpus owner still settling contradictions mid-season and the table covering four branches out of everything the desk gets asked. Years two through five run at full rate, which is the right shape here rather than an optimistic one, because the population resets every spring by the company's own published hiring pattern, so the tool meets a fresh novice cohort every March instead of decaying into a habit nobody uses. Compounding is real on the retained assets and is NOT modelled, the canonical policy source and the vessel map get better each season they are maintained and we take no credit for that. The recommended smaller ask ramps faster, 70 percent in year one, because the paper tally sheet starts in the final nine weeks of the 2026 season and the canonical source is usable the day it is signed off.

scenarios.conservative: 6 first-season desk agents, 12 novice hours and 4 veteran hours each over weeks one to six, 25 and 30 percent of those hours removed, 6 wrong-clock refunds a season at two adults on the lowest verified fare, 50 percent of them prevented, a 22,000 dollar gated option with a 35 percent chance the gate fails, 20 percent contingency, 30 percent year-one ramp. THIS CASE DOES NOT CLEAR AT 18,000. It recovers roughly a third of five-year TCO and we expect roi_math.py to return no payback inside the horizon.
scenarios.most_likely: 10 first-season desk agents, 20 novice hours and 7 veteran hours each, 40 and 45 percent removed, 14 wrong-clock refunds a season at two adults on the 6 Hour fare, 70 percent prevented, a 30,000 dollar gated option at a 50 percent chance of failing, 18 percent contingency, 45 percent year-one ramp. This case clears, and it clears thinly, with payback deep in year four. A thin most-likely case is not a strong buy signal and we are not going to call it one.
scenarios.aggressive: 15 first-season desk agents, 30 novice hours and 11 veteran hours each, 55 and 60 percent removed, 26 wrong-clock refunds a season at two adults on the highest verified fare, 85 percent prevented, a 38,000 dollar gated option at a 60 percent chance of failing, 15 percent contingency, 60 percent year-one ramp. This case clears comfortably and it rests almost entirely on an error frequency nobody has ever counted. The spread between conservative and aggressive is more than tenfold, which is the honest signature of a case with no baseline.
scenarios.recommended_ask_conservative: The SAME conservative benefit assumptions applied to a 4,500 dollar Phase Zero with no software in it. This case clears, at the margin, and it is the only version of this engagement whose conservative case clears.

roi.conservative_clears_reasoning: At the 18,000 dollar ask, no. We are saying that in the heading rather than in a footnote, as the economics pre-check required. The quantifiable annual benefit under conservative assumptions lands in the low thousands, the five-year TCO at 18,000 lands near 50,000 once training hours, five years of run cost and 20 percent contingency are in it, and roughly a third of that gets recovered. The verdict is robust: we re-tested it against higher agent counts, a larger cost per refund error and a doubled event frequency, and conservative still fails. It fails for a reason that is a fact about the business rather than a fact about the build, the desk is small and its headcount is unpublished, which is exactly what the conscience gate said before this analysis started. The RECOMMENDED ASK is therefore not 18,000 today. It is about 4,500 dollars for a Phase Zero with no software in it, and the conservative case for that one clears. We want to be blunt about how that 4,500 was arrived at, because a CFO is entitled to suspect it: it is not a bottom-up scope estimate that happened to clear, it is the CEILING the conservative benefit supports, solved for, and the scope was then cut to fit under it. Saying that out loud is the point. Phase Zero is the corpus crawl and the conflict list, facilitated adjudication with a named internal owner producing one dated canonical policy source, the vessel-map workshop with a written abstain rule, the paper tally sheet installed for the final nine weeks of the 2026 season, and the miss-log specification including the PII rule, the held-out split and the supervisor sampling arm. The 18,000 dollar decision table is not withdrawn, it is RE-PRICED against a measured baseline in autumn 2027, when the tally sheet has produced the denominator this analysis did not have. If the counted error frequency lands anywhere near the most-likely assumption, the 18,000 dollar build clears conservatively at that point and we will show the arithmetic again with real numbers in it.
roi.payback_range: Reported as a range and never as a point, and every month figure is computed by scripts/roi_math.py rather than narrated here. At the 18,000 dollar ask we expect the range to run from NO PAYBACK INSIDE FIVE YEARS in the conservative case, through payback deep in year four most-likely, to somewhere in year two aggressive. At the recommended 4,500 dollar Phase Zero ask we expect conservative payback near the end of the five-year horizon, which is honest rather than attractive, and which is why the case for Phase Zero rests on the decision it buys rather than on its payback speed. Two calendar adjustments the reader must apply and which the script does not model. First, month zero is GO-LIVE, so the four-month build and reconciliation period that precedes March 2027 sits before month one and pushes every calendar date out by about four months. Second, benefit only accrues while a season runs, March 7th to October 11th, so a payback month is a position on a benefit curve that is flat for roughly five months of every year. Where this section and the script disagree, THE SCRIPT WINS and this sentence is the defect.
roi.base_rate_note: The outside view first, stated at full strength rather than as a hedge. MIT's finding is that about 95 percent of generative AI pilots produce no measurable P&L impact. RAND puts AI project failure at about 80 percent, roughly double the rate for non-AI IT projects. Reference-class forecasting says the right prior for this build is that it does nothing, and an inside-view estimate written by the people who would be paid to do the work is exactly the estimate that prior exists to correct. Six specific things put this build in the small share that pays, and the first one is the strongest. ONE, THE FUNDED SCOPE CONTAINS NO MODEL. It is a deterministic decision table over a finite, already-published input space, so the dominant failure mode in that 95 percent, a probabilistic system whose real-world error rate nobody measured, is absent by construction rather than managed. TWO, the acceptance bar is 100 percent agreement across an EXHAUSTIVE ENUMERATION of the input cross product, certified rather than sampled. Almost nothing in AI can be certified, and this can. THREE, it FAILS CLOSED. Any input combination not in the table returns no published rule for this case, escalate to the named role, and writes a miss-log entry. It never interpolates and never guesses, and the accessibility branch abstains outright whenever the vessel serving a departure is not known with certainty. FOUR, it is aimed at the population where the strongest available evidence concentrates its effect, novices, with near zero effect on experienced workers, and it deliberately does not target the 22-year vice president or the 15-year maintenance director. A rollout to everyone would dilute into an average that looks like failure while the tool worked exactly as measured. FIVE, the baseline is a NAMED DELIVERABLE rather than an assumption, so the variance check can actually run, and a case that plans to be checked is the marker the failure literature keeps identifying. SIX, the next spend is gated on a number that can fail against us and we have written down that we do not invoice if it fails. Now the counterweight, which belongs in the same paragraph rather than in a softer one further down. Design does not beat a base rate on its own, execution does, and the single largest risk here is not technical at all. It is that nobody at Major Marine runs a paper tally for nine weeks. If that happens the outcome is unmeasurable, and unmeasurable is not a smaller claim, it is a different kind of claim, and the study says so rather than promising a measured result.
roi.value_owner: PROPOSED, and they assign it, we do not. The number should sit with ONE named person on their side and we propose the Director of Shoreside Operations, Kirsten McNeil, at 11 years, because the check-in office and the reservations desk are inside that remit and because a value owner who does not control the workflow cannot move the number. Two supporting owners, each named because the analysis fails without them. The Operations Manager, Tayja Wright, at 8 years, runs the paper tally sheet for the final nine weeks of the 2026 season and re-runs it in the same calendar weeks of 2027, which is the entire measurement apparatus. A named internal POLICY owner adjudicates every corpus contradiction and signs the one dated canonical source, and we propose the Director of Sales, Kori Goertz, because pricing and package rules sit in that role, and because only somebody inside the company knows which parking price is the right one. That last role is not optional and it is not ours to fill. Alaska AI owns the build and the arithmetic. Alaska AI does not own the adoption, and pretending otherwise is how the 95 percent gets made.
roi.variance_check: Baseline first, because there isn't one today. The paper tally sheet runs from now to October 11th, 2026, the final nine weeks of the season, recording question asked, time to answer, escalated or not, and to whom. Zero software and zero cost. It is re-run in the SAME CALENDAR WEEKS of 2027 so the comparison is season-matched rather than calendar-matched, which matters on an operation whose volume is shaped entirely by the season. Four checks at that point. ONE, the three operational metrics, median time to answer, escalation rate for first-season agents, and count of policy misquotes reaching a guest, all three of which must fall with no fall in guest experience. TWO, the cash check, counted generous-direction refund errors in 2027 against the 2026 tally, reported whether it moved or not, and this is the check that decides whether the 18,000 dollar build is ever worth buying. THREE, the miss log counted against all three parts of the gate, 15 percent outside the table, 20 distinct types recurring three or more times, 150 labelled items after de-duplication, published as a result either way. FOUR, a re-run of this exact ROI model with the counted numbers substituted for the assumed ones, with every driver that moved named and the direction it moved in. One guard against ourselves, written down now rather than later. The party that designs the table is the party that determines what counts as a miss, and a narrower table produces a fatter miss log. The table's boundaries are therefore agreed with the client UP FRONT, and the supervisor logs every question on two randomly chosen full days a month so the log has an arm that is not selected by us or by a busy agent.
what_would_make_this_wrong: THE TALLY SHEET NEVER RUNS. This is the largest risk in the whole case and it is not a technical one. Every driver in this model is an assumption, the tally sheet is the only thing that converts any of them into a measurement, and it is their work rather than ours. If it does not run, the honest position is that the outcome can't be measured, and we say so instead of promising a measured result.

THE REFUND ERROR FREQUENCY IS LOWER THAN 6 A SEASON. That single driver moves this analysis more than any other. If the desk almost never quotes the wrong clock, the cash strand collapses, the whole case rests on capacity hours that are not payroll reductions, and the correct answer is that they should not buy the decision table at any price. We would rather find that in September 2026 than in March 2027.

THE DESK SHARE OF THE 60 SEASONAL HIRES IS SMALLER THAN ASSUMED. About 60 seasonal employees is verified from their own employment page. The share who work the reservations desk is UNPUBLISHED, and we assumed 10 to 25 percent. Deckhands, cooks, engineering and dock support are the bulk of a boat operation. If the desk is three people and two of them return every year, both ramp lines shrink toward nothing.

THE VESSEL-TO-DEPARTURE MAP TURNS OUT NOT TO BE STABLE. If vessel assignment moves with maintenance and charters, the accessibility branch never ships, the table covers three branches rather than four, and every cut percentage in the ramp lines is too high.

THE LOADED HOURLY RATES ARE WRONG. Nothing about their pay is published. We assumed 26 to 34 dollars loaded for a seasonal agent and 42 to 58 for a veteran or supervisor, built up from an assumed wage plus payroll burden plus the real employer-side cost implied by their own published housing and travel support. If the true loaded rate is lower, both capacity lines shrink proportionally.

THE CAPACITY LINES GET READ AS CASH. They are not cash and we have labelled them capacity in every place they appear. If a reader mentally converts freed hours into a smaller payroll, the case looks roughly twice as good as it is. On a fixed seasonal cohort hired inside a fixed window, that conversion is simply not available.

THE GATED OPTION IS PRICED WRONG. The 22,000 to 38,000 dollar range for the retrieval option is our own assumed scope rather than a quote, and we chose to use our own number precisely because a vendor average would be worthless as this company's baseline. If that option would really cost far less, the decision-data line shrinks and the recommended Phase Zero ask stops clearing.

WE PRICED PHASE ZERO BY SOLVING FOR THE CEILING. The 4,500 dollar figure is the largest ask the conservative benefit supports, solved for, with the scope then cut to fit under it. That is a legitimate way to size an ask and it is also exactly the move Flyvbjerg warns about, so it is disclosed here rather than presented as a coincidence. If the scope cannot honestly be delivered for 4,500, the ask does not go up, the recommendation becomes the free tally sheet alone.
assumptions: NO BASELINE EXISTS. Median time to answer, escalation rate and policy-misquote count are recorded nowhere at this company today. Reservations desk headcount, annual passenger volume and call volume are all unpublished. Every driver below is a STATED ASSUMPTION and not a measurement, and no hours-saved case is built on an unpublished headcount denominator anywhere in this model.

pursuits_per_year, meaning first-season desk agents a year, assumed at 6 conservative, 10 most-likely, 15 aggressive. Chosen as roughly 10, 17 and 25 percent of the verified about 60 seasonal employees, on the assumption that Customer Service and Sales Staff, which their own employment page lists first among six role categories, covers the phone desk plus the check-in office plus the dock ticket window, and on the further assumption that most of that group is new each spring given a hiring window of January 15th to April 15th. Confidence LOW on the split, MODERATE on the annual rebuild.

hours_per_pursuit on the novice line, assumed 12 conservative, 20 most-likely, 30 aggressive, over weeks one to six. Built from an assumed 20 questions per agent per day across roughly 30 shifts, with an assumed extra 2 to 4 minutes per lookup on the share of questions that need a policy page. Confidence LOW.

hours_per_pursuit on the veteran line, assumed 4 conservative, 7 most-likely, 11 aggressive, of veteran time consumed per first-season agent over the same six weeks. Chosen at roughly a third of the novice figure on the assumption that most lookups are self-served and only the harder ones escalate. Confidence LOW.

rate on the novice line, assumed 26, 30 and 34 dollars an hour fully loaded. Built from an assumed base wage plus assumed payroll burden plus the real employer-side cost implied by their own published employee housing from 15 dollars a night and a 400 dollar out-of-state travel reimbursement, whose magnitude is unpublished. Confidence LOW. This is an assumption, never a fact, and it is not an industry average.

rate on the veteran line, assumed 42, 50 and 58 dollars an hour fully loaded for a returning senior agent, supervisor or manager. Confidence LOW, chosen deliberately below what a director-level interruption is actually worth so the line cannot be accused of inflation.

cut on the novice line, assumed 0.25, 0.40 and 0.55, and on the veteran line 0.30, 0.45 and 0.60. Bounded well under 1.0 because the funded table covers only four branches out of everything the desk is asked, and because the veteran line has the cleaner mechanism, a lookup removes the go-ask-somebody step more completely than it removes reading time. Confidence LOW.

events_per_year on the refund line, assumed 6 conservative, 14 most-likely, 26 aggressive. THIS IS THE DRIVER THAT MOVES THE ANSWER and it has no denominator, because booking volume is unpublished. 6 a season is roughly one every five weeks of a 31-week season, chosen as a floor rather than a middle. Confidence VERY LOW and stated as such wherever this number appears.

cost_per_event on the refund line, assumed 298, 478 and 618 dollars, constructed identically across all three scenarios as TWO ADULTS at a verified adult fare, 149 dollars on the 4 Hour conservative, 239 on the 6 Hour most-likely, 309 on the 8.5 Hour aggressive. Party size of two is assumed. The transportation component of a transportation package is UNPUBLISHED and is excluded entirely, which understates all three figures. Confidence MODERATE on the fares because they are verified, LOW on party size.

reduction on the refund line, assumed 0.50, 0.70 and 0.85. Bounded by ADOPTION rather than by tool accuracy, because the table itself is certified at 100 percent agreement across an exhaustive enumeration and the refund branch has no abstain path, its inputs are booking contents the agent enters by hand. Confidence MODERATE.

cost_per_event on the decision-data line, assumed 22,000, 30,000 and 38,000 dollars for the gated snippet-retrieval option. This is OUR OWN assumed scope, used deliberately in place of any vendor or industry figure. It excludes the multi-year run cost of the option that never gets built, which understates the line. Confidence LOW.

reduction on the decision-data line, meaning the probability the three-part gate FAILS on measured evidence, assumed 0.35, 0.50 and 0.60. Conservative here means a LOW probability, because a failing gate is what creates the benefit. There is a real argument that 0.35 is too low, since 150 labelled items after de-duplication is a demanding bar on a small desk and under-logging at peak is guaranteed, and we left it low on purpose. Confidence LOW.

events_per_year on the decision-data line, set at 0.23 conservative and 0.22 in the other cases. This is a MODELLING CONVENTION, not a frequency. The decision is a one-time event at the end of the 2027 season, and 0.22 to 0.23 a year annualizes to almost exactly one occurrence across the five-year horizon under each scenario's ramp multiplier. It is disclosed here because a reader who took it literally would be misled.

The reconciliation line, assumed 900, 1,600 and 2,600 dollars a year of current ad-hoc effort at an assumed 45 dollar loaded rate, times an assumed 0.40, 0.55 and 0.65 removed. The reduction is stated NET of the maintenance hours already carried inside run cost, so the same work is not counted on both sides of the ledger. The underlying defect rate is verified rather than assumed, four independent freshness and consistency defects found in one afternoon of external reading of a corpus of roughly thirty pages. Confidence MODERATE on the defects, LOW on the effort figure.

implementation set at 18,000 dollars in all three scenarios, exactly the fixed-price phase one ask from the economics pre-check, never adjusted upward anywhere in this model. The fourth scenario sets it at 4,500 for the recommended Phase Zero.

training set at 3,500, 4,600 and 6,200 dollars, which is entirely THEIR hours and not an invoice. About 84 hours in year one at the conservative population, itemised in cost_note. It rises in the aggressive case because a larger desk means more onboarding and more labelling, which keeps the scenarios internally consistent rather than letting the aggressive case get cheaper as it gets bigger.

run_cost_per_year set at 4,800, 3,600 and 2,800 dollars, and 1,000 for the recommended Phase Zero. There is ZERO inference cost and ZERO token cost because the funded build has no model in it. What remains is the pre-season regression re-run and content refresh before March 7th each season, hosting and tooling, and the policy owner's review cadence. Season scoping makes the refresh annual and non-optional, because two seasons are live at once. Confidence MODERATE.
run_cost_years set at 4.5 of the 5-year horizon in every scenario, the mid-year go-live convention used by scripts/roi_math.py.

contingency set at 0.20 conservative, 0.18 most-likely, 0.15 aggressive, inside the 15 to 20 percent band. Top of the band conservative because the failure risk here is organizational rather than technical, the tally sheet and the corpus owner and the vessel map are all their work.

year1_ramp set at 0.30, 0.45 and 0.60, and 0.70 for the recommended Phase Zero. This is ADOPTION and not calendar. The build lands with the March 2027 cohort so year one contains one full season, and the discount reflects a new tool in the hands of a new cohort with the corpus owner still settling contradictions mid-season. Phase Zero ramps faster because the paper tally sheet starts in the final nine weeks of the 2026 season and the canonical source is usable on sign-off.
years set at 5 in every scenario, per the Gartner five-year TCO horizon.
The change-fee benefit, a 15 dollar per person re-booking fee forgone, is EXCLUDED on purpose despite being verified, because it is immaterial and a weak fifth line makes the whole stack weaker.

The staff-engineer design and product-manager metrics files were not on disk at the time this analysis was written. It is built on claims.json, the locked pick with its economics pre-check, and the conscience gate's feasibility file, and every driver above should be re-checked against the design and the PRD before the study ships.
roi.tco_notes: Four notes for whoever runs the arithmetic. ONE, the drivers object below carries FOUR scenarios, not three. The first three all sit at the 18,000 dollar ask so the reader sees that ask evaluated honestly under every assumption set. The fourth, recommended_ask_conservative, applies the SAME conservative benefit assumptions to the smaller Phase Zero ask, and it exists because the role requires the recommended ask to be one whose conservative case clears, and because saying what ask size it clears at is only auditable if the drivers are on the table. scripts/roi_math.py iterates over whatever keys are in scenarios, so all four compute. TWO, every derived figure comes from that script and none of it is narrated here. Where a sentence in this file and the script output disagree, the script wins and the sentence is the defect. THREE, the payback month the script returns is measured from GO-LIVE, so the four-month build and reconciliation period before March 2027 sits before month one and every calendar date moves out by about four months. The script also spreads benefit evenly across twelve months, which is wrong on an operation whose season runs March 7th to October 11th, so the curve is really flat for about five months of every year. Both adjustments are stated rather than modelled. FOUR, no single hero number appears anywhere in this file and none should appear in the study. The conservative case at 18,000 does not clear, and that sentence belongs in the ROI section's heading per FIELD_STUDY_SPEC, not in a footnote.
